title: Starbucks is ‘not buying Chipotle’ after report it had explored a deal
summary: Starbucks said that it would not be moving to buy Chipotle Mexican Grill, after a report days earlier said the coffeehouse chain had evaluated the prospect.
story: Starbucks said Monday that it would not be moving to buy Chipotle Mexican Grill, after a report last week said the coffeehouse chain had evaluated the prospect.
“As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on rumors and speculation, but we want to be clear we are not buying Chipotle,” a Starbucks spokesperson told NBC News in an email.
“Our team is laser focused on executing our Back to Starbucks strategy,” they said, while adding that the company looked forward to sharing its latest financial results later in October.

The announcement from Starbucks came after the Financial Times reported Thursday that “Starbucks has explored a takeover of Chipotle Mexican Grill.” The report also said that it had hired advisers to work on a takeover proposal for Chipotle.
Starbucks responded to the report later Thursday by issuing a statement that did not definitively address the status of its interest in Chipotle.

A deal between Starbucks and Chipotle would have been transformative for the restaurant and fast-casual dining sector. It would have also reunited Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol with Chipotle, the company he led until late 2024.
For Subscribers
In the immediate aftermath of the FT report, Starbucks shares fell, while Chipotle’s stock surged sharply higher.
For Subscribers

But over the past year, the two companies have been on different trajectories. Starbucks is in the midst of a vast turnaround program, which Niccol has touted in recent weeks as delivering progress. Over the past year, Starbucks shares have risen 15%.

On the other hand, Chipotle’s shares have plunged 20% over the past 12 months. Both companies are grappling with broadly higher prices for consumers and lagging traffic and are trying to revive sales.
Chipotle did not immediately respond to a request for comment Monday.

title: To counteract a spooky economy, America prepares to spend on Halloween candy
summary: This Halloween, rising prices for groceries and gas are pushing many consumers to cut back. But they’re not giving up Halloween candy.
story: This Halloween, the fright isn’t just at the haunted house. Rising prices for everything from groceries to gas are driving many consumers to cut back.
“I’m walking to save a little bit of money,” said Lakisha Reardon, a legal assistant. “I’m bringing in my own lunch.”
Reardon said she has especially seen her electric bill spike this year. She said she is paying an extra $150 every month.
“I’m ready to invest in candles,” she said.
But one thing she won’t give up? Halloween candy.
Average prices for chewing gum and candy have soared 8.1% over the last year, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
Despite the higher prices, Americans are still buying treats.

“I remember being a little kid and being super excited when I would get Reese’s Cups,” said Abby Mynatt, a college student who lives in Knoxville, Tennessee. “I want to give that to some other children.”
Mynatt, 21, said she usually spends around $50 for Halloween candy. She is expecting to shell out a bit more money this year despite financial pressures.
“I certainly think there are a little more tense things with my budget right now,” she said. “But I still think that certain things, even just little pleasures, are still worth it.”
The price of nonchocolate candy items has averaged $3.31 this year, up 1.8% from last year, according to PwC. But Halloween chocolate prices have jumped 15.5%, to an average of $5.67 per package.
Industry experts attribute the rise in chocolate prices partly to a cocoa shock over the last couple of years.

Extreme weather in key cocoa-producing countries like Ivory Coast and Ghana sent global cocoa prices soaring — they quadrupled from January 2023 to January 2025, according to data from the International Monetary Fund.

“Because chocolate makers buy cocoa months, sometimes up to two years ahead, shoppers are paying for that spike now,” said Ali Furman, PwC’s consumer markets industry leader. “Cocoa prices have since fallen by about half, but lower costs take time to reach the shelf and won’t show up on shelves this Halloween season.”
The market research firm NIQ has seen a more muted increase in prices, with chocolate overall up 9.4% from a year ago but Halloween-specific chocolate just up 1.7%.
Analysts say tariffs this year aren’t helping, either. In July, the U.S. imposed tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on 60 trade partners.

“Chocolate comes from elsewhere, so tariffs being added onto it have certainly increased costs that manufacturers are feeling as well,” said Chris Costagli, the leader of food and nonalcoholic beverage insights at NIQ.
Still, the National Retail Federation projects that Halloween spending will soar to $13.5 billion this season, with 96% of Halloween shoppers expecting to buy sweets.
For Subscribers
It’s part of a broader trend this year of consumers leaning into little luxuries like makeup and movie tickets as an antidote for economic gloom.
For Subscribers

A lot of that gloom stems from concerns about inflation and the rising cost of living. Consumer prices have jumped 3.4% over the last year in large part due to rising energy costs, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
With wages up just 3% over the same period, paychecks aren’t keeping up with prices.
It has led many people to forgo bigger purchases and cut back in small ways every day.
Leonard Smith is planning to buy Halloween candy this year, but says he may cut back.
“I don’t want to spend that much money because I need money for other things besides candy,” said Smith, 36, who lives in Delaware.
But he has a strategy to save: Smith buys candy after Halloween when many stores slash prices.

Ari Monahan, a nanny who describes herself as “like a Disney adult, but for Halloween,” said she may get candy that’s a little less expensive, but she still wants to treat the kids in her New York City neighborhood.
“I want to be the good house,” she said. “There’s not that many kids in my area, so I want to give them a little prize for coming.”
Monahan, 30, also buys little treats for herself. “Dark chocolate, a lot of coffees, anything pumpkin spice,” she said.

“If it makes me smile and I have a little money, I’ll pay for it because everything is so grim right now,” she added. “A pair of socks with dachshunds on it, I’m like, ‘You know what? I can do that. I could swing it today.’”
Monahan says rising prices are taking a big bite out of her paycheck, and she worries she might never be able to buy a house.

Home prices are near record highs, and mortgage rates have spiked over the course of the war with Iran — with the 30-year fixed rate topping 7.6% earlier this month, a nearly three-year high. It’s a double whammy that is putting a key pillar of the American Dream further out of reach for many people.
And yet in an economy where the big things might seem far away, there are always little treats to get by.
“I’ve been in a real ‘buy yourself little treats’ mentality,” said Monahan. “I keep buying too much stuff for my dog. I guess I didn’t buy another dog. That’s saving, right?”

title: What’s the White House press pool?
summary: The Justice Department is investigating the five TV networks that make up the White House TV press pool. Here’s how the pool works.
story: The Justice Department’s decision to investigate the five TV networks that make up the White House television pool for potentially violating antitrust laws has thrust the decades-old press pool system into the spotlight.

The investigation comes after Trump last month barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House grounds. The TV pool members responded by declining pool coverage for four days initially, and then on two subsequent occasions when CNN was blocked from performing its pool duties. That meant there was limited video coverage of Trump for six days, including his summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and his travel to New York for the United Nations General Assembly.

While the Justice Department investigates, the three news outlets CNN, MS NOW and Politico are challenging the Trump policy in federal court, in a case with implications for the longstanding system that journalists in the U.S. and around the world rely on to report on the presidency.
What is the press pool?

The White House press pool is a group of media outlets that share video, editorial information and costs for coverage of high-profile officials and events involving the president anywhere in the world. Under the system, the day’s designated “poolers” represent the wider press corps to document newsworthy events and serve as a conduit between the president and the public.
The arrangement allows the pool to distribute video and information to its members in situations where space is limited, such as events in the Oval Office or Cabinet meetings.
DOJ investigates TV networks over Trump pool coverage
The White House press corps has separate print, radio, still photography and TV pools. Press pools cover high-profile administration officials, government departments and government events.

The TV press pool declined to provide video and editorial coverage of Trump before a federal judge temporarily blocked the ban while a lawsuit filed by the three affected outlets proceeds. The TV pool also declined to provide coverage on subsequent days when the White House barred CNN from Air Force One, preventing the network from carrying out its scheduled pool duties.
But TV poolers have continued to cover other administration officials, including Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who did not join in the ban on specific news outlets.
How does it work?

Poolers track the president, giving the public insight into his events, speeches and even his health. For example, video shot by the TV pool captured the moment Trump was shot at a 2024 rally; later, footage of his bruised hand sparked questions about his health.

A press pool typically travels alongside the president anytime he leaves the White House, including when he’s vacationing or dining out. Before the age of social media, the president’s proximity to the press pool was one of the only ways to immediately deliver a message to Americans, such as during a sudden national crisis.

Poolers have reported on scheduled and spontaneous major stories that shaped the course of history. Former WHCA President Steven Portnoy wrote that poolers were in the motorcade when President John F. Kennedy was shot. They witnessed the attempted assassination of President Ronald Reagan, and they covered President George W. Bush during the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.
Who is part of the TV pool?

The network television pool consists of the five major networks: NBC, ABC, CBS, CNN and Fox. The networks take turns sending a journalist and camera crew to both scheduled and spontaneous administration coverage.

The designated pooler distributes editorial content and video feeds widely to the other networks and pool subscribers, which can include outlets that may not have the resources to shoot and distribute coverage themselves. Pool subscribers include outlets like Newsmax, One America News Network, NewsNation and C-SPAN.

International outlets can also subscribe to the pool, allowing them to use network-shot video and editorial guidance in their coverage around the world. When world leaders visit, as Xi did this week, the pool includes a slot for foreign media. Print, radio and still images are represented by their own separate pools.
How did the pool system begin?
The pool system has been in place for decades across both Democratic and Republican administrations.
Reporters used a pool system to cover the presidency as early as the World War II era, when poolers traveled with Franklin D. Roosevelt, according to the White House Correspondents’ Association.
Who controls the TV pool’s content?

The journalists who comprise the pool determine the content of the coverage. The White House can shoot and distribute its own video, but the pool system provides content independent of the administration in power.

The five networks that comprise the TV pool make daily coverage decisions about which network is covering an event for the pool and how it is being covered. The networks are regularly in contact with each other to coordinate pool coverage.

The Trump administration also created a “secondary TV pool” position. However, while the position allows an outlet invited by the White House to participate in coverage where space is limited, the “secondary” pooler only reports for their outlet, not the wider pool of journalists. They do not distribute video or editorial content to pool subscribers.
Has the White House banned specific media outlets before?
This appears to be the first time a president has moved to ban three major media outlets from White House grounds.

While the White House Correspondents’ Association traditionally determined which outlets would be allowed to serve in the print pool, television networks have overseen the TV pool. The Trump administration, though, has at times moved to block outlets.

For example, the administration moved to block The Associated Press from accessing the Oval Office and Air Force One last year after it refused to change its style for the Gulf of Mexico after Trump renamed it the “Gulf of America;” the AP’s legal challenge to the ban is ongoing. Separately, the administration removed The Wall Street Journal from the pool of media outlets traveling to Scotland with Trump in 2025 in response to the newspaper’s report about an alleged birthday card the president sent Jeffrey Epstein in 2003.

In 2018, during his first term, Trump temporarily withdrew credentials from then-CNN reporter Jim Acosta after a contentious interaction at a press conference — but did not move to limit CNN’s access as a news outlet. A judge temporarily ordered the administration to restore Acosta’s credentials, and days later, the administration permanently restored his pass.

And while the president is expected to always travel with pool reporters, Trump evaded the pool when he took a secret flight out of Turkey this summer. The president entered Air Force One, where the pool and other journalists were waiting. The president, though, slipped onto another plane via a catering truck amid security concerns related to the war in Iran.

title: Coast-to-coast cleanup after three storms batter North America
summary: North Americans are dealing with the aftermath of three storms that battered the continent’s coasts this weekend.
story: North Americans are dealing with the aftermath of three storms that battered the continent’s coasts this weekend.
Hurricane Isaias made landfall Friday near Destin, Florida, as a Category 2 storm. It forced evacuations along the Florida Panhandle and in some areas of Alabama.

At least four people were killed in the storm, including Jennifer Williams, whose family said she died when a tree fell into her home. Her husband, Joey, told NBC News that a tree hit their Pensacola home, crushing their family room and killing her instantly.

At least one other person was killed due to a downed tree in Alabama. Another died of carbon monoxide poisoning from a generator running in his garage in Florida, and a fourth person was killed in a motor vehicle crash in Alabama, The Associated Press reported.

title: Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home searched by federal agents in criminal probe
summary: Federal agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home in Washington, D.C., on Monday morning, according to two people familiar with the investigation.
story: Federal agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home in Washington, D.C., on Monday morning, according to two people familiar with the investigation.

One of the people familiar with the probe said the search is part of a yearslong criminal investigation by Homeland Security Investigations, the U.S. attorney in Minneapolis and the Department of Justice. The probe, which involves whistleblowers, documents and witness testimony, deals partly with immigration and fraud, but goes beyond those things, the source said.
A Justice Department spokesperson said in a statement that Homeland Security Investigations “executed a judicially authorized search warrant as “part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation.”
The statement did not specify that the warrant was related to Omar, D-Minn., or provide further information about the nature of the investigation.

In a post on X, Omar called the search “an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” adding that over the last decade, President Donald Trump “has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”

House Democratic leaders said in a joint statement that the search was “deeply disturbing and raises serious questions about the continued corrupt weaponization of the federal government against Donald Trump’s adversaries.”

Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, Minority Whip Katherine Clark of Massachusetts and Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar of California vowed in the statement to “deliver full accountability for the rogue abuse of power from the Department of Homeland Security and Department of Justice.”
The search was first reported by Fox News. The White House and Department of Homeland Security referred questions about the search to the Justice Department.

Trump has frequently lashed out at Omar, who is a member of a progressive faction of women in Congress collectively known as the “squad,” criticizing her over her liberal positions and saying she should “go back” to where she came from.
Omar, who is running for re-election in Minnesota, immigrated to the U.S. from the war-torn country of Somalia as a child in the 1990s.

The timing of Monday’s search puts it under added scrutiny: There are 22 days until the midterm elections, and a long-standing Justice Department practice tells prosecutors to be especially careful about actions near an election that could appear to help or hurt a candidate.

There is no blanket rule barring the department from acting within 60 days before an election, but that’s long been an unwritten practice. The written policy says prosecutors and agents cannot time investigative steps or public statements to influence an election and directs them to seek guidance when the timing could raise questions.

That guidance is not always followed. In 2016, then-FBI Director James Comey publicly disclosed developments in the email probe of Democratic presidential nominee Hillary Clinton just 11 days before the presidential election.
For Subscribers

After he took office, Trump fired Comey, and the administration justified his dismissal by saying he had violated long-standing principles of the Justice Department by announcing his conclusions about the Clinton case. Trump said he would have fired Comey “regardless” of the Justice Department memo outlining what it said were his missteps.

Early in Trump’s second term, Justice Department officials used the prospect of election interference as a basis to throw out a corruption case against former New York City Mayor Eric Adams in federal court in Manhattan. Adams’ indictment for bribery and campaign finance violations was filed about a year before the 2025 mayoral election, during former President Joe Biden’s tenure.

But under Trump, then-acting Deputy Attorney General Emil Bove moved in February 2025 to dismiss the case, writing the move was necessary in part because of “risks of interference” with the city’s upcoming elections — a highly controversial push that led to the resignation of the acting U.S. attorney overseeing the matter.
For Subscribers

Late last month, the Justice Department’s Office of the Inspector General recommended that the department’s leaders prioritize giving guidance to agents and prosecutors on actions that could “foreseeably affect an impending election.”

Those include “the taking of overt investigative steps, indictments, public announcements, or other actions” that could have such an impact, according to the recommendation, which was initially part of a 2018 report on the DOJ and FBI’s actions leading up to the 2016 election.
Last month, border czar Tom Homan told Fox News that Omar was being investigated by the Department of Homeland Security.

“If someone committed immigration violation, if someone committed marriage fraud or anything like that, regardless if they’re a congressman or not, no one’s above the law,” Homan said at the time. “So, I’ll leave it at that. We’ll let HSI, Homeland Security Investigations, continue the investigation.”
Omar fled Somalia’s civil war with her family when she was 8 years old and stayed in a Kenyan refugee camp for four years before moving to the U.S., her website details.
Ahead of Monday’s news, Trump again targeted both Omar and Somalis over the weekend during his remarks at a rally in Tennessee.
“How about Ilhan Omar? She comes from Somalia,” he said Saturday as the crowd booed.
The president went on to characterize the country as ungoverned and lawless, saying “all they have is crime and squalor.”

“What they’ve done to Minnesota, these people from Somalia, what they’ve done to Minnesota should never be allowed,” he added. “And let’s see what happens. JD Vance and our people are looking at it very strongly.”

Early this year, Trump said that the Justice Department and Congress are “looking at” the congresswoman. The president has also repeatedly targeted Minnesota over fraud scandals that roiled the state.
Last week, Trump told Minnesotans to “fight back” against Somali immigrants, claiming in a Truth Social post that the state “is being taken over by Somali Immigrants.”

One of the most high-profile fraud cases the alleged theft of $250 million from a Covid-related program that provided food for children. Since then, the Justice Department announced criminal charges against more than a dozen people in Minnesota over alleged social services fraud.

The former leader of Feeding Our Future, the nonprofit at the center of the $250 million fraud case, is white. Most of the defendants in the related cases are of Somali descent, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office, a fact Trump has highlighted as he has repeatedly disparaged people of Somali descent.
Omar blamed Trump’s rhetoric against her and Somali immigrants as a contributing factor in an attack on her at a town hall event in January.

title: Deadly Saudi airport strikes mark major Mideast escalation
summary: Fears of intensifying conflict were growing in Saudi Arabia on Monday after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis launched multiple strikes on Riyadh’s airport over the weekend, killing 13 people and wounding hundreds.
story: RIYADH, Saudi Arabia — Fears of intensifying conflict were growing in Saudi Arabia on Monday after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis launched multiple strikes on Riyadh’s airport over the weekend, killing 13 people and wounding hundreds.
“What is clear is we remain on a strong escalation ladder,” said Adam Baron, a fellow at New America, a Washington, D.C.-based think tank, who follows Yemen and the wider Gulf region.

More than 300 people were injured when the kingdom’s main international airport was attacked Saturday, marking a major escalation in the Houthi rebel group’s campaign against the world’s leading oil exporter and key U.S. ally in the region.

Among the victims were one American, as well as four citizens of Saudi Arabia, two Bangladeshi nationals, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Palestinian, a Syrian and one Sudanese national. The Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia later said that an Indian national injured in Saturday’s attack had died.
Video capturing the Saturday attack showed a packed airport before the flash of an explosion sends people running for safety as debris falls on them.
The airport remained shut Monday.
The impact of the attacks were felt at the WPC Energy Congress in the Saudi capital Monday, with several top energy executives dropping off the event’s schedule.

The chief executives of Exxon Mobil, TotalEnergies, Shell, Chevron and BP had all been expected at the event, which started Sunday, but were no longer on the agenda that conference organizers released early Monday, Reuters reported. The energy giants did not immediately respond to requests for comment from NBC News.

“You know this country is safe and that we hold your protection at whole heart,” Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said, according to Reuters, as he opened Monday’s session of the gathering held just miles away from Riyadh airport. But, he added, “our gathering here does not mean the risk is gone.”
He said the stepped-up fighting was serious and that the kingdom’s response must be “equally serious.”
“There is no way that somebody will break our back. We are like a phoenix,” he separately said. “We come out of the ashes all the time and every time.”

Fighting on the ground in neighboring Yemen is also intensifying, with the Houthis expanding their operations along its Red Sea coast and around the Bab el Mandeb, a key shipping route connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.
Saudi Arabia and the Houthis began fighting in 2015 after the kingdom entered Yemen’s civil war on behalf of the internationally recognized government.

A period of relative calm following a 2022 ceasefire was shattered in July when the Houthis resumed attacks after accusing Saudi Arabia of striking Sanaa airport as a plane from Iran was attempting to land.

Baron said the latest attacks — the deadliest by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia in more than a decade — could have a “galvanizing effect” on Washington and other international actors, including Pakistan and Turkey, which recently reached a joint defense agreement with the kingdom.
Saudi Arabia defiant following multiple strikes on Riyadh

“As these attacks are growing stronger and stronger, on the one hand, it’s increasing the hurt on the kingdom, but it’s also increasing assessments for many that there has to be some strong effort to degrade the Houthis and restore deterrence,” Baron said.
Washington faces mounting pressure. President Donald Trump on Saturday said he was still weighing whether to join in Saudi Arabia’s military operations against the Houthis.
“We may. We’re gonna look at it,” he told reporters. “We just found out about the recent attack. So we’ll make a decision. We move very quickly.”

After sweeping gains by Houthi forces in Yemen last month, Trump said the rebel group had contacted the U.S. to stress that it doesn’t “want to fight with us” and would “much prefer not having us involved.”
While the skies over Riyadh were empty Monday after flights in and out of the capital were canceled, roads were full of traffic as residents tried to get back to normal life.
And in the early hours of Sunday, road crossings at the border with the United Arab Emirates were largely deserted.

“With the Houthis, we knew that they could hit Riyadh airport, but it’s almost about the precision,” Baron said. “There’s a great degree of anxiety in terms of ... living in a world where you can just have random armed groups hitting airports.”

title: Pope Leo to be hospitalized Tuesday for surgery to remove a lung nodule
summary: Pope Leo XIV will be admitted to a hospital Tuesday morning to undergo surgery to remove a lung nodule discovered during recent medical tests, the Vatican said Monday.
story: Pope Leo XIV will be admitted to a hospital Tuesday morning to undergo surgery to remove a lung nodule discovered during recent medical tests, the Vatican said Monday.
The timing of the procedure was confirmed after the 71-year-old American pontiff had a full day of meetings, audiences and appointments.
The Vatican press office also said no particular issue precipitated the tests, denying Italian media reports suggesting an inflammation had prompted the medical check-up.
Leo revealed the discovery during his Sunday noon prayer and said he was following doctors’ advice to remove the nodule “in the coming days.” The Vatican predicted a weeklong recovery.

It was business as usual at the Vatican on Monday, with Leo presiding over six private audiences, including with the head of the U.S. military chaplains, Archbishop Timothy Broglio, and one group audience. He also made three appointments, and the Vatican released a letter he had penned to the outgoing dean of the College of Cardinals.
In the afternoon, he was expected to rejoin a weeklong conference he convened on ministering to families.

Leo’s surgery marks the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. It was significant because the pope himself revealed the news, in perhaps the most public way possible: at the end of his Sunday noon blessing, with thousands of people in St. Peter’s Square.
For Subscribers

The Vatican has for centuries zealously guarded the pope’s health and has often sent out confusing information, or none at all, about papal illnesses. Pope Francis tried to change that by being upfront about his frailties and musing on his eventual death. But even during his pontificate, information was tightly controlled.
For Subscribers
Leo’s decision and reveal suggested an unusual level of transparency by the American pope.

A lung nodule is a small abnormal area measuring less than 3 centimeters (1 inch) that sometimes appears on a CT scan of the chest or abdomen. Often, the scans are done to investigate trauma or a lung infection, unrelated to a lung cancer screening. A nodule can be benign or malignant, and oftentimes surgical removal is recommended to ascertain whether it is cancerous since performing a lung biopsy by needle can be difficult.
Oncologists say if the nodule turns out to be cancerous, Leo’s prognosis is “excellent” since it will have been removed at an early stage.

title: NFL Week 5: Don’t count out Aaron Rodgers and Drake Maye just yet
summary: Plus, three undefeated and three winless teams remain after a week of bizarre endings and bounce-back performances.
story: Week 5 of the NFL season featured the latest chapter of one of the game’s most storied rivalries and resurgent performances from Aaron Rodgers and Drake Maye.
Here’s all the action you need to know about from Sunday.
Aaron Rodgers is heating up

After having looked like one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL to start the season, Pittsburgh Steelers starter Aaron Rodgers threw three touchdown passes for the third straight game, this time in a 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts.

The last time Rodgers threw at least three touchdown passes in three straight games was in 2021, during his fourth MVP season with the Green Bay Packers. Rodgers is up to 10 touchdowns and four interceptions this year, and the Steelers improved to 3-2 with the win.
The Packers earn a measure of revenge
The Packers restored some balance in their rivalry with the Chicago Bears, defeating a Caleb Williams-less Bears squad 31-7.

It was the teams’ first matchup since Chicago’s epic comeback in the wild-card round of last year’s playoffs. The Bears had won two in a row in the series, also authoring a come-from-behind win last regular season.

This time, the Packers dominated on both sides of the ball. Green Bay held Ben Johnson’s offense in check, while Jordan Love had his finest game of the season. Love completed 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards, two touchdowns and a season-best 137.5 passer rating.

Johnson has made no secret of his distaste for Green Bay since he took over in Chicago. After a frosty handshake following last winter’s playoff game, Johnson and Packers coach Matt LaFleur had a (relatively) friendly exchange Sunday.
Drake Maye is fully back
After a terrible start to the season, Maye, the New England Patriots quarterback, has now strung together two straight games reminiscent of the player who finished second in MVP voting in 2025.

Maye threw for 374 yards and four touchdowns against the Las Vegas Raiders, also adding a score on the ground in a 45-17 win. In his last two games, he has thrown seven touchdown passes and only one interception.
The Raiders were getting beaten so badly that rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in April’s NFL draft, got his first game action. He completed 6 of 8 passes for 48 yards.
More from the NFL

How the Philadelphia Eagles pulled off the wildest loss of the NFL seasonThe Commanders had seconds left to secure a win — and blew itThe 49ers look like the NFL’s best team after surviving a heavyweight fight
How the Philadelphia Eagles pulled off the wildest loss of the NFL season
The Commanders had seconds left to secure a win — and blew it
The 49ers look like the NFL’s best team after surviving a heavyweight fight
The Vikings stay undefeated
The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 after they beat the New Orleans Saints 23-13. The Vikings continue to ride their defense, as their offense has been inconsistent at best this season.
Quarterback Kyler Murray showed some improvement, however, completing 80% of his passes and posting a season-best 109.6 passer rating in the victory.
Minnesota will play the Colts in Week 6 before its schedule gets tough: The Vikings will play the Detroit Lions, the Buffalo Bills, the Packers and the San Francisco 49ers in November.
The Lions’ window to contend is still open

Two years after the NFC North was the NFL’s best division, it’s full of good but not great teams. Count the Detroit Lions among them. The Lions’ 164 points (a 32.8-point average) are the second most in franchise history through five weeks of a season, but they have needed to score that much to outplay a porous defense allowing 29.6 points.
On Sunday, after punts on their first three drives, the Lions (3-2) scored on their following seven consecutive possessions to easily beat Arizona and earn their first road win this season.
A week of down-to-the-wire endings

Sunday began with a stunner and ended with the season’s fifth overtime. In London, after Philadelphia took a lead with 8 seconds left, Jacksonville returned its ensuing kickoff deep enough to get into field-goal range and also fast enough to leave 1 second on the clock. The Jaguars then kicked a walk-off winning field goal to beat Philadelphia in what Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence called “maybe the craziest game I’ve ever been a part of.”
For Subscribers
Why kick it directly to a returner?
“I lost us that game,” Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said.

Even more inexplicable was Washington’s tie with the New York Giants, when the clock ran out in overtime before the Commanders, who didn’t have a timeout, could stop the clock and kick a field goal. Why allow quarterback Jayden Daniels to run the ball and keep the clock moving with only seconds left? Washington coach Dan Quinn blamed himself.

“Sunday Night Football” on NBC offered an appropriate bookend to a wild day. After Baltimore scored a game-tying touchdown and 2-point conversion with 40 seconds left in regulation, Atlanta couldn’t muster a game-winning drive when quarterback Michael Penix Jr. was hit hard and knocked out of the game. In the season’s fifth overtime game, Baltimore scored first and Atlanta had one final opportunity to match. But backup quarterback Tua Tagovailoa threw an interception on Atlanta’s second play, and the Ravens (4-1) hung on 30-23.
And then there were ...
... three undefeated teams and three winless teams left.
For Subscribers

San Francisco survived by inches to win in Seattle in one of the best games of the season to start 5-0 for the fifth time in the Super Bowl era. On the other end of the standings, Houston (1-4) and Tampa Bay (1-4) both earned their first wins during Week 5. Still searching for their own are Miami, Tennessee and the Los Angeles Chargers, all 0-5.

The Chargers put together yet another performance full of either botched plays or bad luck, depending on your perspective, including a fumble by quarterback Justin Herbert when his own lineman’s foot accidentally kicked the ball out of his hand midway through the fourth quarter. The Chargers never led again after that turnover.

summary: Experts weigh in on vibration plates and whether they can help you workout and lose weight.

Never heard of them? “A vibration plate, also known as a power plate, is a machine that vibrates when you stand on it,” says John Gallucci Jr., a doctor of physical therapy and CEO of JAG Physical Therapy. “This forces your muscles to constantly contract and relax.”

Unlike sneakers, stationary bikes or ankle weights, vibration plates seem a bit more complicated to use. And do they even work? To answer these questions and more, I spoke with physical therapists — here’s what they had to say.

Do vibration plates work?

With so many ridiculous wellness fads out there, I was skeptical when I first started seeing videos of people standing on these vibrating devices pop up in my feed. So, the first question I asked the experts I spoke with was whether they actually have any benefits. The answer: They may. There is some truth to their effectiveness — but research behind them is mixed, so it those benefits may not be quite as strong as the hype suggests, says Thomas R. Denninger, a physical therapist at ATI Physical Therapy.

So what do vibration plates actually do? “They cause your muscles to quickly tighten and relax over and over, as they are working to keep your balance,” says Denninger. “Because your body has to work a little harder to stay steady, you may feel like your whole body is working.” Here are some of the potential benefits, according to Denninger:

They can help your muscles turn on and work harder, especially during simple exercises like squats or bridges.Because the surface is shaking, your body has to constantly adjust. While all of these benefits are possible with regular use, Denninger stresses that a vibration plate should not replace regular exercise. “Think of it more as a workout booster, not a cure-all,” he says.

How to shop for a vibration plate
If you are interested in adding a vibration plate to your workout routine, experts I spoke with recommend keeping the following in mind as you shop:

Type: There are three different types of vibrations. Frequently asked questions

There are several optimal times to use a vibration plate. They can warm up muscles before a warmout, during a workout to make moves like squats and planks more challenging or after a workout to help alleviate stiffness, says Denninger. When it comes to how often you should use a vibration plate, Gallucci suggests using it for 10 to 20 minutes a few times a week.
And just to be safe: anyone who is pregnant, has a pacemaker, certain heart conditions, or joint instability should talk to a provider before using one. Denninger

Vibration plates are relatively safe and can be used by just about everyone. “They are suitable for those looking to improve strength, balance and flexibility, and those recovering from certain injuries,” says Gallucci. That said, people who are pregnant are better off not risking losing their balance. title: How to clean your dryer to keep it working longer, according to experts
summary: For the best way to clean a dryer, and to learn more about how often to do it, I talked to home cleaning experts for their recommendations and guidance.
story: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends (and questions) on our timelines, like whether bath sheets are actually different from towels.

It makes sense that you may never think about cleaning your dishwasher or washing machine, since unlike the stuff you wash in them, you don’t interact with them much. The same could be said for your dryer, but just like the aforementioned appliances, your dryer does need to be cleaned from time to time.

Cleaning home appliances that you use nearly every day keeps them functioning properly and saves you money. Think about it: A few dollars for products and an hour of your time now spares you from paying a repairperson later, or worst case scenario, needing to replace your dryer altogether.

How to clean a dryer
Follow the expert-recommended steps below for cleaning your dryer. Consider using the products above to help.

While you don’t have to clean the entire dryer that often, it’s most important that you regularly clean the lint trap (the screen in the lining of the door) regularly, according to Ryan Knoll, founder of home cleaning company TidyCasa. Aside from simply wiping away the lint, you can do things to clean it more thoroughly, he says.

To clean the lint trap and the compartment it slides into, use the crevice and hose attachment tool from your vacuum or a hose attachment kit, like the Holikme Dryer Vent Cleaner Kit with Lint Vacuum Attachment & Brush, to clean the lint on the screen. Then use it to clean the inside of the compartment. You can also use a long bristle brush, like the one included in the Holikme kit, to clean the lint on the inside of the compartment.

To clean the dryer vent and exhaust duct, you’ll need a long bristle brush and a wide brush that you can attach to a long rod, such as from the Holikme Dryer Vent Cleaner Kit, to be able to reach the inside of the duct. The kit includes a nylon rod that attaches to a power drill, so that you can put the brush attachments inside the duct and rotate it to lift the lint before using the vacuum and hose suck it out.
How often do you need to clean your dryer?

Cleaning the screen that traps lint frequently is most important, according to Knoll. “Clean the lint trap every time before or after you use the dryer,” says Knoll. “Clean the dryer vent itself every two to three years. We’re talking deep hose clean-out, either sucking lint out or pushing it through the vent.” The dryer vent includes the exhaust duct (the silver hose-like structure made from aluminum) on the back.
Can a dryer cause a fire?

Yes, the lint that collects in and around the dryer vent and lint trap can block air from the dryer and, in addition to preventing your clothes from drying, can lead to a fire, according to Becky Rapinchuk, owner of cleaning brand and site Clean Mama*. This is why she recommends cleaning the screen frequently, including with warm water and soap.

“Vacuum the lint trap housing regularly. Clean the dryer vent hose or duct at least once or twice a year to keep airflow strong and drying times short,” she says. “Wipe the drum occasionally, and clean the moisture sensors (inside the drum) with a little rubbing alcohol on a cloth to remove residue that causes inaccurate dryness sensing.”
*Any product recommendations in this story were made independently of Rapinchuk, who we only consulted for guidance. We did not ask her for product recommendations.
How do you know if your dryer needs to be cleaned?

Make a note of how your clothes feel after drying them once — they may still be damp after drying for a long time. “If your dryer isn’t drying your clothes as well as it used to, that’s a good sign it needs a cleaning,” says Knoll. This is because lint is trapped on the screen of the dryer vent, which stops air from getting through and drying clothes properly, according to Knoll.

title: Food pantries overwhelmed by Trump cuts
summary: Those on the front lines of feeding their neighbors in rural West Virginia say they face unprecedented challenges brought on by Washington.
story: DUNLOW, W.Va. — Bill Likens stared down a half-mile-long line of cars that started forming before the sun came up over the Appalachian Mountains. He had one job: figure out how to feed them all.

Some had driven more than 30 miles in aging cars and trucks that wheezed down flood-prone roads through the steep hills. They sat silently as the temperature rose into the 80s, their vehicles turned off with no air conditioning to preserve gas, waiting hours for a few boxes of food.

Aided by a cane, Likens, 51, surveyed the pallets being unloaded off a semitruck that arrived that morning. He counted cartons of eggs and sacks of potatoes to calculate how much each waiting car could get — an algorithm of hunger he is constantly trying to solve.

title: To counteract a spooky economy, America prepares to spend on Halloween candy
summary: This Halloween, rising prices for groceries and gas are pushing many consumers to cut back. But they’re not giving up Halloween candy.
story: This Halloween, the fright isn’t just at the haunted house. Rising prices for everything from groceries to gas are driving many consumers to cut back.
“I’m walking to save a little bit of money,” said Lakisha Reardon, a legal assistant. “I’m bringing in my own lunch.”
Reardon said she has especially seen her electric bill spike this year. She said she is paying an extra $150 every month.
“I’m ready to invest in candles,” she said.
But one thing she won’t give up? Halloween candy.
Average prices for chewing gum and candy have soared 8.1% over the last year, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
Despite the higher prices, Americans are still buying treats.

“I remember being a little kid and being super excited when I would get Reese’s Cups,” said Abby Mynatt, a college student who lives in Knoxville, Tennessee. “I want to give that to some other children.”
Mynatt, 21, said she usually spends around $50 for Halloween candy. She is expecting to shell out a bit more money this year despite financial pressures.
“I certainly think there are a little more tense things with my budget right now,” she said. “But I still think that certain things, even just little pleasures, are still worth it.”
The price of nonchocolate candy items has averaged $3.31 this year, up 1.8% from last year, according to PwC. But Halloween chocolate prices have jumped 15.5%, to an average of $5.67 per package.
Industry experts attribute the rise in chocolate prices partly to a cocoa shock over the last couple of years.

Extreme weather in key cocoa-producing countries like Ivory Coast and Ghana sent global cocoa prices soaring — they quadrupled from January 2023 to January 2025, according to data from the International Monetary Fund.

“Because chocolate makers buy cocoa months, sometimes up to two years ahead, shoppers are paying for that spike now,” said Ali Furman, PwC’s consumer markets industry leader. “Cocoa prices have since fallen by about half, but lower costs take time to reach the shelf and won’t show up on shelves this Halloween season.”
The market research firm NIQ has seen a more muted increase in prices, with chocolate overall up 9.4% from a year ago but Halloween-specific chocolate just up 1.7%.
Analysts say tariffs this year aren’t helping, either. In July, the U.S. imposed tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on 60 trade partners.

“Chocolate comes from elsewhere, so tariffs being added onto it have certainly increased costs that manufacturers are feeling as well,” said Chris Costagli, the leader of food and nonalcoholic beverage insights at NIQ.
Still, the National Retail Federation projects that Halloween spending will soar to $13.5 billion this season, with 96% of Halloween shoppers expecting to buy sweets.
For Subscribers
It’s part of a broader trend this year of consumers leaning into little luxuries like makeup and movie tickets as an antidote for economic gloom.
For Subscribers

A lot of that gloom stems from concerns about inflation and the rising cost of living. Consumer prices have jumped 3.4% over the last year in large part due to rising energy costs, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
With wages up just 3% over the same period, paychecks aren’t keeping up with prices.
It has led many people to forgo bigger purchases and cut back in small ways every day.
Leonard Smith is planning to buy Halloween candy this year, but says he may cut back.
“I don’t want to spend that much money because I need money for other things besides candy,” said Smith, 36, who lives in Delaware.
But he has a strategy to save: Smith buys candy after Halloween when many stores slash prices.

Ari Monahan, a nanny who describes herself as “like a Disney adult, but for Halloween,” said she may get candy that’s a little less expensive, but she still wants to treat the kids in her New York City neighborhood.
“I want to be the good house,” she said. “There’s not that many kids in my area, so I want to give them a little prize for coming.”
Monahan, 30, also buys little treats for herself. “Dark chocolate, a lot of coffees, anything pumpkin spice,” she said.

“If it makes me smile and I have a little money, I’ll pay for it because everything is so grim right now,” she added. “A pair of socks with dachshunds on it, I’m like, ‘You know what? I can do that. I could swing it today.’”
Monahan says rising prices are taking a big bite out of her paycheck, and she worries she might never be able to buy a house.

Home prices are near record highs, and mortgage rates have spiked over the course of the war with Iran — with the 30-year fixed rate topping 7.6% earlier this month, a nearly three-year high. It’s a double whammy that is putting a key pillar of the American Dream further out of reach for many people.
And yet in an economy where the big things might seem far away, there are always little treats to get by.
“I’ve been in a real ‘buy yourself little treats’ mentality,” said Monahan. “I keep buying too much stuff for my dog. I guess I didn’t buy another dog. That’s saving, right?”

title: What’s the White House press pool?
summary: The Justice Department is investigating the five TV networks that make up the White House TV press pool. Here’s how the pool works.
story: The Justice Department’s decision to investigate the five TV networks that make up the White House television pool for potentially violating antitrust laws has thrust the decades-old press pool system into the spotlight.

The investigation comes after Trump last month barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House grounds. The TV pool members responded by declining pool coverage for four days initially, and then on two subsequent occasions when CNN was blocked from performing its pool duties. That meant there was limited video coverage of Trump for six days, including his summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and his travel to New York for the United Nations General Assembly.

While the Justice Department investigates, the three news outlets CNN, MS NOW and Politico are challenging the Trump policy in federal court, in a case with implications for the longstanding system that journalists in the U.S. and around the world rely on to report on the presidency.
What is the press pool?

The White House press pool is a group of media outlets that share video, editorial information and costs for coverage of high-profile officials and events involving the president anywhere in the world. Under the system, the day’s designated “poolers” represent the wider press corps to document newsworthy events and serve as a conduit between the president and the public.
The arrangement allows the pool to distribute video and information to its members in situations where space is limited, such as events in the Oval Office or Cabinet meetings.
DOJ investigates TV networks over Trump pool coverage
The White House press corps has separate print, radio, still photography and TV pools. Press pools cover high-profile administration officials, government departments and government events.

The TV press pool declined to provide video and editorial coverage of Trump before a federal judge temporarily blocked the ban while a lawsuit filed by the three affected outlets proceeds. The TV pool also declined to provide coverage on subsequent days when the White House barred CNN from Air Force One, preventing the network from carrying out its scheduled pool duties.
But TV poolers have continued to cover other administration officials, including Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who did not join in the ban on specific news outlets.
How does it work?

Poolers track the president, giving the public insight into his events, speeches and even his health. For example, video shot by the TV pool captured the moment Trump was shot at a 2024 rally; later, footage of his bruised hand sparked questions about his health.

A press pool typically travels alongside the president anytime he leaves the White House, including when he’s vacationing or dining out. Before the age of social media, the president’s proximity to the press pool was one of the only ways to immediately deliver a message to Americans, such as during a sudden national crisis.

Poolers have reported on scheduled and spontaneous major stories that shaped the course of history. Former WHCA President Steven Portnoy wrote that poolers were in the motorcade when President John F. Kennedy was shot. They witnessed the attempted assassination of President Ronald Reagan, and they covered President George W. Bush during the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.
Who is part of the TV pool?

The network television pool consists of the five major networks: NBC, ABC, CBS, CNN and Fox. The networks take turns sending a journalist and camera crew to both scheduled and spontaneous administration coverage.

The designated pooler distributes editorial content and video feeds widely to the other networks and pool subscribers, which can include outlets that may not have the resources to shoot and distribute coverage themselves. Pool subscribers include outlets like Newsmax, One America News Network, NewsNation and C-SPAN.

International outlets can also subscribe to the pool, allowing them to use network-shot video and editorial guidance in their coverage around the world. When world leaders visit, as Xi did this week, the pool includes a slot for foreign media. Print, radio and still images are represented by their own separate pools.
How did the pool system begin?
The pool system has been in place for decades across both Democratic and Republican administrations.
Reporters used a pool system to cover the presidency as early as the World War II era, when poolers traveled with Franklin D. Roosevelt, according to the White House Correspondents’ Association.
Who controls the TV pool’s content?

The journalists who comprise the pool determine the content of the coverage. The White House can shoot and distribute its own video, but the pool system provides content independent of the administration in power.

The five networks that comprise the TV pool make daily coverage decisions about which network is covering an event for the pool and how it is being covered. The networks are regularly in contact with each other to coordinate pool coverage.

The Trump administration also created a “secondary TV pool” position. However, while the position allows an outlet invited by the White House to participate in coverage where space is limited, the “secondary” pooler only reports for their outlet, not the wider pool of journalists. They do not distribute video or editorial content to pool subscribers.
Has the White House banned specific media outlets before?
This appears to be the first time a president has moved to ban three major media outlets from White House grounds.

While the White House Correspondents’ Association traditionally determined which outlets would be allowed to serve in the print pool, television networks have overseen the TV pool. The Trump administration, though, has at times moved to block outlets.

For example, the administration moved to block The Associated Press from accessing the Oval Office and Air Force One last year after it refused to change its style for the Gulf of Mexico after Trump renamed it the “Gulf of America;” the AP’s legal challenge to the ban is ongoing. Separately, the administration removed The Wall Street Journal from the pool of media outlets traveling to Scotland with Trump in 2025 in response to the newspaper’s report about an alleged birthday card the president sent Jeffrey Epstein in 2003.

In 2018, during his first term, Trump temporarily withdrew credentials from then-CNN reporter Jim Acosta after a contentious interaction at a press conference — but did not move to limit CNN’s access as a news outlet. A judge temporarily ordered the administration to restore Acosta’s credentials, and days later, the administration permanently restored his pass.

And while the president is expected to always travel with pool reporters, Trump evaded the pool when he took a secret flight out of Turkey this summer. The president entered Air Force One, where the pool and other journalists were waiting. The president, though, slipped onto another plane via a catering truck amid security concerns related to the war in Iran.

title: South Carolina Senate rivals spar over Iran, AI and Trump in debate
summary: Annie Andrews and Darline Graham are running to replace the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, and the winner will make history as the first female senator elected from South Carolina.
story: Republican Sen. Darline Graham of South Carolina and Democratic challenger Annie Andrews clashed Sunday night in their first and perhaps only debate of the general election, tangling over President Donald Trump’s “one big, beautiful bill,” the high costs of gas and goods, the Iran war and AI data centers.

South Carolina is a ruby-red state where Trump remains popular among Republican voters. But the race has tightened in the closing stretch of the campaign, and Democrats believe they have a shot at knocking off Graham, who was appointed to fill her brother Lindsey Graham’s Senate seat after his sudden death in July. The top Senate Republican super PAC has pledged to spend $5 million to shore up Graham’s campaign.
At the start of the debate, hosted in Columbia by South Carolina ETV, Darline Graham noted that Sunday night marked exactly three months since her brother unexpectedly died at age 71.

Andrews, a pediatrician, sought to portray Graham, who previously led a state agency, as an inexperienced empty suit who refuses to stand up to Trump or his unpopular policies. She mocked Graham as “the White House’s ambassador to South Carolina.”

Graham attacked Andrews as the “most radical liberal” to run in South Carolina and as sympathetic to the Democratic Socialist Party. “Annie Andrews will not stand up to the Socialist Democratic Party; she’s only going to join them,” Graham said — a characterization Andrews rejected.

Graham has “been told to come out here and call me Bernie, Ocasio, Mamdani — that’s what’s in her script. But the truth is my name is Annie Andrews, and there shouldn’t be any confusion about that,” Andrews said. “The truth is I support the Second Amendment, I believe we need a secure border, and we need to deport illegal immigrants who break the law. ... The real difference between me and Sen. Graham is that I will stand up to my own party, and I will always put South Carolina first.”

Graham and Andrews are running for a full six-year Senate term; the winner will make history as the first female senator elected from South Carolina. The debate also featured Libertarian Kasie Whitener.
For Subscribers

Graham and Andrews tussled over issue after issue. As the country faces Social Security insolvency, Andrews said she would raise caps to make wealthier people pay more but would not hike the retirement age. She added that Republicans like Graham want to privatize Social Security so “Washington insiders” can profit. “Unfortunately, my opponent is in the race to do what Washington insiders tell her,” she said.

Graham shot back that she understands what people in her state are facing. When her parents died at a young age, Social Security benefits helped her and her brother survive. Graham said Andrews’ criticism of Trump’s “one big, beautiful bill” is misplaced because it lowered taxes on tips and Social Security. “You called it the one big, ugly bill, so here you are deceiving the people of South Carolina,” Graham said.

On affordability, Graham said she has “lived paycheck to paycheck” before and acknowledged that “gas prices are high right now. ... I feel the pain, too.” She said that she supports suspending the gas tax and that easing regulations on drilling would permanently bring prices down.
Andrews pinned blame for high gas prices on Graham, who she said voted several times against a war powers resolution to restrict Trump’s war with Iran.
For Subscribers

“The war is the exact reason we now have record-high gas and diesel prices. Farmers are getting crushed, and everything costs more,” Andrews said. “My opponent is the only one who had the opportunity to vote to end the war, but three times in a row she voted to continue it.”

Andrews also dinged Graham for admitting during a previous debate that “national security is not my thing.” “South Carolina, if your surgeon said that appendectomies aren’t really his thing, would you still hand him a scalpel? No,” Andrews said. “So why would we hand Darline Graham a full term in the U.S. Senate? She is unserious and unqualified.”
Graham retorted that she wants the war to end, like everyone does, but said she believes in “peace through strength.” Then, she went after Andrews over the national security quip.

“But talking about not my thing, let’s talk about what’s not your thing. Your thing apparently is not being honest with the people of South Carolina. At least I’m honest. If I don’t know something, I am glad to say it, and I’ll say it again tonight,” Graham said without getting specific. “But you have, you are deceiving the people of South Carolina. You have flip-flopped on everything. There’s so many social media posts out there to prove it. Shame on you!”
The proliferation of data centers, which power artificial intelligence companies, has become a major flash point in the midterm elections.

Andrews went right after Graham on the issue, nicknaming her “Data Center Darline.” Andrews said her data-center plan calls for a “two-year moratorium, protections to ensure your rates don’t go up and a return to real local control.”

Graham fired back that stopping construction of all data centers would allow China to win the race for AI dominance. She said she voted for the Ratepayer Protection Act, which aims to shift higher energy costs from building data centers from consumers onto AI companies.

“Under her Bernie Sanders plan, a two-year moratorium, that is dangerous to the national security of our country, because in two years China is going to be so far ahead [that] we are going to be in so much trouble,” Graham said, adding that local communities should decide whether data centers get built in their backyards.
“I want communities to decide. She wants the federal government to decide.”

title: NFL Week 5: Don’t count out Aaron Rodgers and Drake Maye just yet
summary: Plus, three undefeated and three winless teams remain after a week of bizarre endings and bounce-back performances.
story: Week 5 of the NFL season featured the latest chapter of one of the game’s most storied rivalries and resurgent performances from Aaron Rodgers and Drake Maye.
Here’s all the action you need to know about from Sunday.
Aaron Rodgers is heating up

After having looked like one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL to start the season, Pittsburgh Steelers starter Aaron Rodgers threw three touchdown passes for the third straight game, this time in a 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts.

The last time Rodgers threw at least three touchdown passes in three straight games was in 2021, during his fourth MVP season with the Green Bay Packers. Rodgers is up to 10 touchdowns and four interceptions this year, and the Steelers improved to 3-2 with the win.
The Packers earn a measure of revenge
The Packers restored some balance in their rivalry with the Chicago Bears, defeating a Caleb Williams-less Bears squad 31-7.

It was the teams’ first matchup since Chicago’s epic comeback in the wild-card round of last year’s playoffs. The Bears had won two in a row in the series, also authoring a come-from-behind win last regular season.

This time, the Packers dominated on both sides of the ball. Green Bay held Ben Johnson’s offense in check, while Jordan Love had his finest game of the season. Love completed 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards, two touchdowns and a season-best 137.5 passer rating.

Johnson has made no secret of his distaste for Green Bay since he took over in Chicago. After a frosty handshake following last winter’s playoff game, Johnson and Packers coach Matt LaFleur had a (relatively) friendly exchange Sunday.
Drake Maye is fully back
After a terrible start to the season, Maye, the New England Patriots quarterback, has now strung together two straight games reminiscent of the player who finished second in MVP voting in 2025.

Maye threw for 374 yards and four touchdowns against the Las Vegas Raiders, also adding a score on the ground in a 45-17 win. In his last two games, he has thrown seven touchdown passes and only one interception.
The Raiders were getting beaten so badly that rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in April’s NFL draft, got his first game action. He completed 6 of 8 passes for 48 yards.
More from the NFL

How the Philadelphia Eagles pulled off the wildest loss of the NFL seasonThe Commanders had seconds left to secure a win — and blew itThe 49ers look like the NFL’s best team after surviving a heavyweight fight
How the Philadelphia Eagles pulled off the wildest loss of the NFL season
The Commanders had seconds left to secure a win — and blew it
The 49ers look like the NFL’s best team after surviving a heavyweight fight
The Vikings stay undefeated
The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 after they beat the New Orleans Saints 23-13. The Vikings continue to ride their defense, as their offense has been inconsistent at best this season.
Quarterback Kyler Murray showed some improvement, however, completing 80% of his passes and posting a season-best 109.6 passer rating in the victory.
Minnesota will play the Colts in Week 6 before its schedule gets tough: The Vikings will play the Detroit Lions, the Buffalo Bills, the Packers and the San Francisco 49ers in November.
The Lions’ window to contend is still open

Two years after the NFC North was the NFL’s best division, it’s full of good but not great teams. Count the Detroit Lions among them. The Lions’ 164 points (a 32.8-point average) are the second most in franchise history through five weeks of a season, but they have needed to score that much to outplay a porous defense allowing 29.6 points.
On Sunday, after punts on their first three drives, the Lions (3-2) scored on their following seven consecutive possessions to easily beat Arizona and earn their first road win this season.
A week of down-to-the-wire endings

Sunday began with a stunner and ended with the season’s fifth overtime. In London, after Philadelphia took a lead with 8 seconds left, Jacksonville returned its ensuing kickoff deep enough to get into field-goal range and also fast enough to leave 1 second on the clock. The Jaguars then kicked a walk-off winning field goal to beat Philadelphia in what Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence called “maybe the craziest game I’ve ever been a part of.”
For Subscribers
Why kick it directly to a returner?
“I lost us that game,” Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said.

Even more inexplicable was Washington’s tie with the New York Giants, when the clock ran out in overtime before the Commanders, who didn’t have a timeout, could stop the clock and kick a field goal. Why allow quarterback Jayden Daniels to run the ball and keep the clock moving with only seconds left? Washington coach Dan Quinn blamed himself.

“Sunday Night Football” on NBC offered an appropriate bookend to a wild day. After Baltimore scored a game-tying touchdown and 2-point conversion with 40 seconds left in regulation, Atlanta couldn’t muster a game-winning drive when quarterback Michael Penix Jr. was hit hard and knocked out of the game. In the season’s fifth overtime game, Baltimore scored first and Atlanta had one final opportunity to match. But backup quarterback Tua Tagovailoa threw an interception on Atlanta’s second play, and the Ravens (4-1) hung on 30-23.
And then there were ...
... three undefeated teams and three winless teams left.
For Subscribers

San Francisco survived by inches to win in Seattle in one of the best games of the season to start 5-0 for the fifth time in the Super Bowl era. On the other end of the standings, Houston (1-4) and Tampa Bay (1-4) both earned their first wins during Week 5. Still searching for their own are Miami, Tennessee and the Los Angeles Chargers, all 0-5.

The Chargers put together yet another performance full of either botched plays or bad luck, depending on your perspective, including a fumble by quarterback Justin Herbert when his own lineman’s foot accidentally kicked the ball out of his hand midway through the fourth quarter. The Chargers never led again after that turnover.

title: Shane Gillis Faces Backlash for ‘SNL’ Monologue Joke About Women’s Gym Attire
summary: Standup comedian Shane Gillis has come under fire for delivering what many people are calling a misogynistic monologue when he hosted “Saturday Night Live.”
story: Standup comedian Shane Gillis has come under fire for delivering what many people are calling a misogynistic joke about the way women dress at the gym during his “Saturday Night Live” monologue.
Gillis, who hosted the Oct. 10 episode of the sketch comedy show, began the bit by explaining how difficult it is for him to work out at a health club.

“Going to the public gym as a fat guy, especially in New York, is a nightmare, dude. It’s just the hottest gay guys you’ve ever seen. They’re jacked, and they look at me like, ‘Yeah, right.’ I know, dude,” he began.

“Also, I haven’t been to the gym in so long. I didn’t know women just dressed like whores now,” he continued. “Look, I’m sorry. There’s no other way to describe — have you seen it? I’ve seen it. The shorts. Have you seen the shorts?
Social media lit up with people blasting Gillis.
“Women wearing shorts at the gym does not make them whores. It makes the men calling them whores misogynists,” Emmy-winning “Schitt’s Creek” star Dan Levy said in an Instagram reel.
“I’m speechless that something like that can exist on live national television,” he added.
Comedian Phoebe Robinson posted a video of herself reacting to the joke.
“Women are dressed like whores? What is the joke?” she said in part.
BuzzFeed Editorial Director Spencer Althouse described the monologue on X as “very awkward,” while another viewer wrote, “This is so disgusting.”

“I don’t know what turns my stomach more, the fact that Shane Gillis was on Saturday Night Live tonight and said women at the gym ‘dress like whores’ or that there was people in that audience who found his disgusting bit of so-called humor funny,” someone else wrote on X.
“have you at any point considered that women are tired of being called ‘whores’ for existing in public,” another user replied to someone on X who said the monologue was “funny.”
Feminist writer Jessica Valenti also posted a TikTok video about the joke in the context of the investigation into a rape allegation at Cornell University, captioning it, “I am LIVID.”
“Shane Gillis knows that there is a major national conversation happening right now about sexual assault,” Valenti said in part.
“And so I don’t want to hear a single f------ word about how this was just in bad taste, this was a mistake, he didn’t realize, it was just tone deaf. No,” Valenti added.
TODAY.com has reached out to representatives for “Saturday Night Live” and Gillis for comment but did not immediately hear back.
In his monologue, Gillis also faced backlash for jokes referring to his older siblings as his “two big fat b---- sisters” and comparing his hairline to Hitler’s.

Gillis’ comedy career has boomed in recent years. In July, he set a Guinness World Record for most tickets sold for a comedy show by a solo comedian. He starred in the comedy series “Tires” and headlined his own comedy special, “Beautiful Dogs,” both on Netflix. He has also appeared in multiple Bud Light commercials.

Gillis has courted controversy with “SNL” before. In 2019, he was fired from the show days after it was announced that he was joining the cast due to resurfaced clips of Gillis using racist slurs and making homophobic jokes on a podcast. Despite his firing, he went on to host “SNL” in 2024 and 2025.
“Most of you probably have no idea who I am … I was fired from this show,” Gillis said in his 2024 “SNL” monologue. “A while ago. But, you know. Don’t look that up, please.”

title: Store Responds After Kelly Clarkson Says Staff Treated Her Like Julia Roberts’ ‘Pretty Woman’ Character
summary: Brooklyn specialty shop Art of Play has responded after singer Kelly Clarkson accused the store of treating her “like Julia Roberts character in Pretty Woman.”
story: Brooklyn specialty shop Art of Play has responded after singer Kelly Clarkson accused the store of treating her “like Julia Roberts character in Pretty Woman.”
Art of Play posted a statement on its Instagram page after Clarkson tweeted on Oct. 10 that she visited the store, with her eye on a few items but instead was “looked at as if I couldn’t afford it.”
Clarkson added that she “was told he could find something comparable for me.”
“Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale,” Clarkson wrote on X, before naming the New York City store.
The small business responded on Oct. 11, saying in a statement that Clarkson had attempted to buy a permanent installation that is not for sale.

“Yesterday, Kelly Clarkson visited us in Brooklyn and inquired about buying ‘Molly,’ a one-of-a-kind singing and dancing bird automaton who plays an important role in the magic shows we host here,” the store wrote on its social media page. “Molly is permanently attached to the wall and isn’t for sale. However, the negative experience Kelly described on twitter would resonate with anyone who has ever felt judged in a shop.”
The store, which wrote that it had become the subject of backlash after Clarkson’s post, thanked those who supported it.

“Thanks to all our friends for their support and welcome to all the curious folks who have discovered us amidst the drama,” Art of Play wrote in the statement, before referencing Clarkson’s hit song. “We’re going to keep our heads down and hopefully, we can clear things up with Kelly someday. As a talented popular singer once said ‘what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger.’”

Clarkson did not immediately respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment. But in another post on X, Clarkson challenged the store’s statement, describing the staff as “not only rude, you’re also a liar.”
“Cool, cool. Sure, it wasn’t for sale. That’s the narrative Art of Play is gonna go with 👍” Clarkson wrote on the social media platform Oct. 11.
The singer then continued with her version of events.

“So the whole conversation we had when I asked you if it was for sale whilst pointing to the price tag hanging on the wall with the title Singing Bird didn’t happen as you elevator eyed me saying in a condescending tone ‘yes, it’s for sale but it costs 15,000 dollars so if you’d like me to find something comparable for you I can.’” she wrote in the post, appearing to convey sarcasm. “That all never happened and now it’s not for sale.”
The singer also hit back at criticisms that she doesn’t support small businesses.

“You don’t get a free pass to treat people less than in your store just because you are a small business,” she wrote. “It’s not that hard to be kind. I never blast people but you my friend were an exception.”
She concluded by saying, “Your store is really cool.”
“Unfortunately, you aren’t,” she wrote.

Art of Play did not immediately respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment on Clarkson’s Oct. 11 post. The store, however, shared a follow-up post to its Instagram early Oct. 12 in an effort to “clarify one additional detail about Kelly Clarkson’s visit.”

“During the 5 minutes she spent in the store, she inquired about our mechanical bird puppet named Molly,” the Oct. 12 post from Art of Play said. “We explained that while Molly is permanently attached to the wall and serves as a de facto mascot for our shop, a nearly identical automaton is owned by the creator of the machines, a brilliant artist named Bliss Kolb who lives in Seattle. He told us he would be willing to part with Molly’s twin for $15,000.”
The store said employees offered to show her another option for a singing bird that was available to take home that day for $2,000 but Clarkson “did not stick around long enough to see it.”
Art of Play said it reached out to the singer directly to “clear the air.”
Art of Play, which sits in the neighborhood of Brooklyn Heights, is a specialty store that features home goods in addition to magic-themed gifts, cards and games.

In her post, Clarkson said that she “drove all the way to Brooklyn” to take a peek at the store, already with a few things in mind to purchase. She compared her experience to that of Julia Roberts’ “Pretty Woman” character Vivian Ward when she is brushed off by a Beverly Hills salesperson who assumes she can’t afford the expensive items in the store because of her casual appearance.
Art of Play said in the statement that the store invites all shoppers to play with their items.
“And they do, many stay for hours enjoying our puzzles, games and toys,” the store said.
The criticisms they’ve been receiving have taken them by surprise, the store said in the statement.

“Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by 8 million people who have never visited our store,” the statement said. “It’s been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity.”

The bird automaton appears to have not been available for purchase in the past. Several weeks ago, the store had made a post about their “favorite items not for sale,” featuring an image of the bird automaton.

Since the parties’ comments, the internet has been divided with Clarkson’s fans flocking to the store’s pages to express their disappointment. Many others, including New York locals, have been commenting as well, sharing their positive experiences with the shop.

title: Ashley Padilla is a Mom Trying To Hold it Together After Babysitter Canceled on ‘SNL’
summary: Ashley Padilla joined the Weekend Update segment of “Saturday Night Live” as a frazzled mom whose babysitter canceled.
story: It’s hard to keep it together when you’ve had it up to here!

Ashley Padilla joined the Weekend Update segment of “Saturday Night Live” as a frazzled mom whose babysitter canceled. Given the circumstances, problem child Coco, played by new cast member Grace Reiter, had to tag along as well.
While the mom tried really, really hard to provide the desk with some cute fall ideas for the family, Coco seemed to have other plans.
“She’s my little buddy tonight because someone just wasn’t getting along with the sitter,” the mom explains during the Oct. 10 episode.
Coco adds with a sinister look in her eyes that she “broke another one.”
