In the sketch, the frazzled mom attempts to share some sweet activities like pressing a leaf into a book — one of her “favorites.”
“Mommy picks a book, and Coco goes and fetches a beautiful orange and red leaf from the yard,” the mom says.
Coco, however, shares how the activity really went down.
“I fell into a pile of leaves, and no one knew where I was for a day,” Coco says.

While the pair bicker, things really unravel when Coco claims she was missing for so long, she didn’t have dinner. According to Coco, the pizza her mom says she ate doesn’t count because she “didn’t like it.”
And mom just loses it.
“It doesn’t matter if you don’t like it,” the mom says, shrieking. “It’s still dinner if you ate it. You ate it all, and that’s dinner because you ate it.”
The mom attempts to share another lovely activity — making dried apple dolls.
“And fun fact: We got the apples just this weekend at a beautiful local apple orchard,” the mom says.
Coco, of course, has something to add.
“My mom stuck me in the corn maze for three hours so she could kiss a farmer,” she says.
Let’s just hope that the mom finally finds a worthy babysitter for Coco. She deserves a break.

title: Ben Affleck Reveals Hilarious Reason Why Matt Damon Passed Up Lead Role in ‘Animals’
summary: Ben Affleck reveals why his best friend, Matt Damon, couldn’t take on the leading role in his new Netflix thriller “Animals” as he had once hoped.
story: Ben Affleck reveals why his best friend, Matt Damon, couldn’t take on the leading role in his new Netflix thriller “Animals” as he had once hoped.

Affleck, who directed and starred in the new movie joined the Oct. 11 episode of Sunday Sitdown to chat about the film. And he revealed that Damon, initially his top pick to star in flick, had some other plans instead.
“I’m sure you’re aware, Ben, you were not the director’s first choice to star in this movie,” host Willie Geist joked.
Affleck confirmed the detail, explaining that Damon got another professional opportunity.

“Matt then ended up getting offered this little, kinda s----- little movie, ‘The Odyssey’ that bombed. And he was very embarrassed by it, of course.” Affleck said, laughing. “It just didn’t work at the box office, or with the critics, which happens sometimes.”
The “Animals” star went on to praise his friend, he played titular character Odysseus.
“He was really as happy as I’ve ever seen him the day that he got that job,” Affleck told Willie of Damon.
Damon and Affleck have been well-known besties, going through their first massive Hollywood moment together as they won the best screenplay Oscar in 1998 for “Good Will Hunting.”
“The whole idea of even being there was absurd,” Affleck recalled to Willie of attending the Oscars. “The year before, we’d watched the show from an apartment in Somerville, Massachusetts.”
The two have since acted in multiple films together including “The Last Duel” in 2021 and “Air” in 2023.

Additionally, Affleck has launched multiple production companies with Damon including Artists Equity, founded in November 2022. The company is behind a number of titles including “Air” and new film “Animals.”

The crime thriller, released Oct. 9, follows a high-profile Los Angeles mayoral candidate whose son is kidnapped, forcing the hopeful and his wife, played by Kerry Washington, into coming up with the $7 million ransom amid a financially stressful time in his campaign.
“I make movies mindful of the audience. But also, I did some things I really wanted to do in this that I think were really interesting,” the actor and director said of the new film.
Affleck beamed over his newest project, “I love this movie, ‘Animals.’ I really want people to see it.”

title: Mike Ditka’s Perfectly Unhinged Version of ‘Take Me Out To The Ballgame’ Resurfaces After Death
summary: A resurfaced video of Chicago Bears icon Mike Ditka singing during the seventh inning stretch at a baseball game is giving many fans something to smile about as they grieve the football giant’s death.
story: A resurfaced video of Chicago Bears icon Mike Ditka singing during the seventh inning stretch at a baseball game is giving many fans something to smile about as they grieve the football giant’s death.
The video features Ditka singing the classic “Take Me Out To The Ballgame” during a July 1998 match at Chicago’s Wrigley Field. And he definitely puts his own twist on the song.

In the clip, shared by MLB, Ditka raucously belts out the words, losing his voice several times throughout the song. Adding to his undeniable aura, Ditka also speeds up, leading the organist to attempt to match his pace.
It’s controlled chaos — just like the beloved football icon himself.
Ditka’s family announced his death Oct. 9. He was 86.

The Bears icon, who led the team to its only Super Bowl victory in  1986, was known for his big personality as much as he was for his gridiron prowess. And that charisma certainly shined during that 1998 Chicago Cubs game against the Pittsburgh Pirates.

That wasn’t even Ditka’s only famous rendition of the ballpark song. During a 2005 game at Wrigley Field between the Cubs and the Philadelphia Phillies, Ditka was joined by comedian Will Ferrell to lead the stadium in the song. The pair, who starred in comedy “Kicking & Screaming,” don’t exactly sing in-sync.

Ditka, who was inducted into the pro football Hall of Fame in 1988, has long been a source of comedy fodder. He even became the focus of a recurring sketch on “Saturday Night Live” in which a group of superfans, who look just like Ditka himself, hail the legendary coach as something of a god.

title: Alexander Skarsgard’s See-Through Dress Shoes Are Causing Chaos Across The Internet
summary: Actor Alexander Skarsgard showed up in a pair of see-through shoes to the annual BFI London Film Festival for an Oct. 8 screening of his upcoming romantic fantasy movie “Wicker.”
story: To call this a bold fashion choice would be an understatement.

Actor Alexander Skarsgard showed up to the annual BFI London Film Festival for an Oct. 8 screening of his upcoming romantic fantasy movie “Wicker.” But his look quickly became a focus of the event as he rocked a pair of see-through oxford shoes on the red carpet.
The shoes unsurprisingly elicited a range of responses from disgust to extreme lust.
Skarsgard’s transparent black shoes, which featured vinyl laces, were paired with a gold, metallic suit.
The oxfords, from fashion house Saint Laurent’s spring 2027 collection, made waves earlier this year when they debuted on the runway at  men’s Paris fashion week in June.

Corrado De Biase, the brand’s freelance design director of shoes, explained that the look is called “O. Fan,” after adult online platform OnlyFans. The shoes, he told Women’s Wear Daily, are a celebration of sexuality in the gay community.

“Because Monsieur Saint Laurent himself was really linked to those young community people when he was young,” De Biase told the outlet. “So it’s normal that a brand like us looks at that kind of thing. It’s been part of the house from the beginning.”
Saint Laurent creative director Anthony Vaccarello had a snarkier explanation for the footwear.
“I asked myself: ‘Why torture women with plastic shoes, but not men?’” Vaccarello said, according to WWD.
People across the internet had their own interpretations of the look. Some couldn’t help but wonder how Skarsgard was faring in the no-doubt sweaty shoes.
Others were just thirsting over the fashion choice.
“Oo our steak is too juicy, our lobster is too buttery, Alexander Skarsgaard is showing too much foot,” one commenter wrote on Instagram.

Well, 2026 appears to be the year of the gutsy red carpet footwear. Margaret Qualley sported a pair of Chanel’s “shoeless shoes” to the world premiere of “The Dog Stars” in August. The shoes were essentially black heels that were strapped to Qualley’s feet with two sets of laces and no soles.
While some deemed the shoes as chic, others joked that the barely-there footwear was a sign of “shrinkflation.”

title: Ben Affleck Admits He Trash Talks Kids Online While Playing ‘Fortnite’
summary: Ben Affleck recently revealed on the “New Heights” podcast that he sometimes gets into squabbles with kids on the internet while playing popular multiplayer open-world survival game “Fortnight.”
story: Gamer rage gets to everyone — even celebs.
Ben Affleck recently revealed on the “New Heights” podcast that he sometimes trash talks kids on the internet while playing popular multiplayer open-world survival game “Fortnight.”
Affleck, it appears, has a tough time taking the heat.

“Twelve-year-olds just f--- you up,” Affleck lamented to hosts Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce on the Oct. 7 podcast episode. “I get killed right away and they taunt you and s--- like ‘You suck! F--- you!’”
Affleck acknowledged that he ends up “getting in arguments” with the kids in the game’s chat.
“F--- you! I don’t suck,” he says in response to the taunting, Affleck told the podcast hosts. “I’m a grown man.”

Affleck, who’s currently promoting crime-thriller film “Animals,” joined the podcast to discuss the project. He explained that the costumes in the film are inspired by some of the outfits, referred to as skins, in “Fortnite.” The video game famously features different skins that can be upgraded through milestones, challenges and more.
As Affleck points out in the podcast, the game has also dropped exclusive and limited edition skins that have become some of the most coveted aspects of the game.
“My son and he’s like ‘For Christmas, can you get me these real skins for Fortnite?’ But they’re 300 bucks,” Affleck tells the podcast of the virtual costumes.
Affleck has long been an avid gamer. On the podcast, he explained that in addition to first-person shooter games, he’s a fan of sports games like football game “Madden” and basketball game “NBA 2K.”

The actor has also been open about his love for “Valorant,” a first-person tactical hero shooter video game. He’s been spotted at major tournaments and even joined a watch party livestream last year with esports team Sentinels.

title: ‘Pretty Little Liars’ Actor Says He Was Held At Gunpoint and Knifepoint in Mugging Attack
summary: Actor Keegan Allen, best known for his role in teen drama series “Pretty Little Liars,” alleges in an Oct. 9 video that he was violently mugged in West Hollywood by two masked men.
story: Actor Keegan Allen, best known for his role in teen drama series “Pretty Little Liars,” alleges in an Oct. 9 video that he was violently mugged in West Hollywood by two masked men.

In the video that was posted to his Instagram account, Allen, who appears to be bleeding from his head, says that he was robbed outside of Laurel Supply, an upscale grocery store in the Los Angeles neighborhood.

“These two dudes hit me in the head and pointed a gun at me with a knife, and then took off,” a visibly bloody Allen, catching his breath, says in the graphic video. He adds that the attackers took his watch.
Responding to comments under his video, the 37-year-old told fans that he went to the hospital following the incident and was “def concussed.”

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department shared a statement in response to an NBC News request for comment on the incident. The department said that the LAPD’s Major Crimes Bureau is investigating the reported Oct. 8 armed robbery.
In the Instagram video, Allen shared footage of the alleged attack, which shows two men pointing a gun at a victim. One of the men bashes the victim over the head.
“Robbed at gunpoint and knifepoint by two young men that threatened to KILL me over my watch and would have! God said no tonight. My life for a watch,” he wrote in the caption of his post.
Allen wrote in response to a comment that one of the attackers also demanded a bracelet the actor was wearing, which led to the beating.
“I was trying to tell him it’s not easy to take off and said ‘you can take it off’ and he pistol whipped me,” Allen wrote.

The sheriff’s department said in the statement that deputies responded to the incident around 9:05 p.m. and spoke to a victim who reported being approached by two male suspects in black clothing. The victim told deputies that one suspect pointed a handgun at him while the other brandished a knife.
Actor Keegan Allen describes violent mugging incident

“During the incident, one of the suspects struck the victim in the face with the handgun, causing a laceration to his forehead,” the statement said. “The suspects took the victim’s watch and fled the location in an unknown vehicle.”
Personnel from the Los Angeles County Fire Department responded to the scene and medically evaluated the victim, who was not transported to the hospital, the statement said.
In his post, Allen called out Los Angeles mayor Karen Bass and California governor Gavin Newsom.
“Let’s hope all these flock cameras that @karenbassla @gavinnewsom and everyone thinks will stop crime can find these very dangerous criminals,” Allen wrote on Instagram.

In a statement sent to NBC News, Bass called the incident “egregious.” She also pointed out that West Hollywood is an independent city and that the LA County Sheriff’s Department is leading the investigation. It is technically not part of the city of Los Angeles.
“No one should have to experience something like this,” Bass said.

According to the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, serious crimes in the area have decreased nearly 10% from January through August. Additionally, robberies have been on the decline. Statistics show that through August, there were 49 reported robberies. That’s a 21% decrease from the 62 incidents during the same period in 2025.
In response to recent October incidents, a department spokesperson said that the agency is increasing the number of deputies conducting patrols throughout the city.
“While these declines are encouraging, they do not diminish the seriousness of recent robberies or the fear felt by our community,” a spokesperson for the department said.

title: There’s a New Britney Spears Song. Listen to ‘She’ll Never Be Me’
summary: Britney Spears fans got an unexpected surprise in the form of a previously unreleased song from the pop icon.
story: Britney Spears fans got an unexpected surprise in the form of a previously unreleased song from the pop icon.
On Oct. 9, Spears and her team dropped the song “She’ll Never Be Me,” which was recorded for her 2001 self-titled third album “Britney.”
The song comes weeks before the album celebrates its 25th anniversary with a special edition re-release, “Britney (25th Anniversary Edition),” that includes songs from the vault.
“She’ll Never Be Me” is a quintessential Britney Spears track with its bubblegum pop, early aughts sound, girl power lyrics and the singer’s signature girlish and gritty vocals.
The 3-minute track talks about a former lover who is now with someone that looks just like her.

“You know I’m one of a kind/Boy, what’s this I see/Your girl, she looks just like me/Blond hair and dressed to a T,” she begins. “You tell me how can this be/Does she know I was the one/Who used to turn you on/But you don’t want to talk about it.”
According to the song’s YouTube description, Spears is credited as the lyricist, associated performer and composer.
Her ex Justin Timberlake is also featured as a lyricist and composer, along with Bradley Daymond and Alex Greggs. Riprock ‘n’ Alex G is a producer.

“She’ll Never Be Me” is one of five new songs included in the “Britney” re-release, including “Am I a Sinner,” “When I Say So,” “My Big Secret” and “Right Now (Taste The Victory)” from her 2002 Pepsi commercial.
Fans will get to hear the songs when “Britney (25th Anniversary Edition)” is released on Nov. 6.
The last time Spears shared a new song was 2023’s “Mind Your Business” with Will.i.am. In 2020, she also dropped a never-before-heard collaboration with the Backstreet Boys titled “Matches.”
The song was featured in a deluxe edition of her 2016 album “Glory.”

title: Crystal Harris Posts Message She Sent Jessica Biel With Plea to ‘Reconsider’ Playing Hugh Hefner’s Wife in Movie
summary: Hugh Hefner’s widow, Crystal Harris, is asking Jessica Biel not to portray a fictional version of the Playboy founder’s wife in the upcoming movie “Playmates.”
story: Hugh Hefner’s widow, Crystal Harris, is asking Jessica Biel not to portray a fictional version of the Playboy founder’s wife in the upcoming movie “Playmates.”

Harris, who was married to Hefner from 2012 until his death in 2017, posted a screenshot of a text on Instagram on Oct. 8 that she sent Biel, urging her to pass up the role of Hefner’s fictional wife.
“Please reconsider playing Hugh Hefner’s ‘wife’ if this film intends to romanticize him or the Playboy world,” Harris wrote in a message to Biel, according to the screenshot she shared on Instagram.

“I was actually his wife, and I experienced sexual, emotional, financial and physical abuse in that relationship. Many other women have come forward with allegations of rape, coercion, drugging and exploitation as well.

“There are also deeply troubling concerns involving minors. I hope everyone involved in this film takes the time to listen to the women who lived it before helping Hollywood turn it back into nostalgia.”
TODAY.com has reached out to Biel for comment about Harris’ post, as well as Harris for any further comment about what she wrote. Neither responded.
TODAY.com also reached out toHefner’s estate for comment about Harris’ allegations of experiencing “rape, coercion, drugging and exploitation,” but did not hear back.
The film is being made by Searchlight Pictures, which not did reply to TODAY.com’s request for comment about Harris’ post or Biel’s casting in the movie.

Variety reported Oct. 6 that Biel has joined the cast of “Playmates,” a coming-of-age story about a 13-year-old girl who befriends a woman competing with other hopefuls to become Playmate of the Month. Bill Pullman, Lily-Rose Depp and Indiana Elle are also attached to star in it.
Biel is slated to play Hefner’s wife in the movie. According to Variety, the character is fictional and not based on a real person.
Hefner was married two other times, to Kimberley Conrad from 1989 to 2010 and Millie Williams from 1949 to 1959.
Harris followed up her post with another one, in which she showed appreciation for the “overwhelming response” she received.
“So many women are speaking up, sharing their experiences, and expressing that they’ve simply had enough,” she wrote.

“Victim blaming is still far too common, especially when it comes to narcissistic and emotional abuse. I know that not everyone has experienced these dynamics firsthand, and I’m genuinely glad for those who haven’t. But I also hope we can listen to and support the women who have, even when their experiences are difficult to understand.”

Harris also said she wants “to support women” and express her hope that the movie is “not something that will glorify Hugh Hefner. With women in the leading roles, my hope is that the film ultimately delivers a message of empowerment: that women can find fulfillment, independence, and a sense of self beyond Playboy.”
In 2024, Harris penned a memoir, “Only Say Good Things: Surviving ‘Playboy’ and Finding Myself,” in which she wrote that living in the famed Playboy Mansion was like living in a prison.

“I always had to be home by six o’clock. If I wasn’t, it was a problem. He would be upset. He would be yelling my name through the house,” she says of Hugh Hefner, writing that she felt like Rapunzel locked in a tower.
“I didn’t know then that I could rescue myself. I didn’t always know I needed to be rescued, but I knew I was trapped,” she added.
Harris also said Hefner was a “narcissist” and had a need to control the women who lived in the mansion.
“It’s like he wanted us to beg him for something, so he could feel even more powerful and probably have us feel small,” she told TODAY.com in 2024.
“It was weird and it was hard. Looking back, he did use me and manipulate me for his own gain in every way,” she continued.
In August, Harris said Hefner was “very abusive” and that she was “brainwashed” when she appeared on the “No One Asked Her” podcast.

“So I just thought I was the crazy one because all of the media put Hef on such a pedestal that I’m like, ‘OK, if they all see him as this larger-than-life amazing human, there must be something wrong with me,” she said.
Hefner has been accused of sexual misconduct before, with multiple allegations leveled against him in the 2022 A&E series “Secrets of Playboy,” released five years after he died in 2017.

“This series contains allegations of wrongdoing over decades by Hugh Hefner and others associated with him,” read a statement at the end of each episode. “The vast majority of allegations have not been the subject of criminal investigations or charges, and they do not constitute proof of guilt.”

title: How Realistic Is ‘War’? A Divorce Lawyer Says this 1 Move Would Get Characters Disbarred
summary: A UK divorce lawyer reacts to the HBO drama “War” including the mole and serving papers on the red carpet.
story: “Take It From Me” is a TODAY.com series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this story, a U.K. divorce lawyer weighs in on “War.”

HBO’s new legal drama “War” gives viewers an unflinching look behind the scenes of a nasty, high-powered divorce. The series focuses on the lengths divorce lawyers from rival law firms in London will go to score a profitable win for their clients.

The depiction of ruthless attorneys scheming to gain the upper hand in a pending divorce “heavily dramatized for viewing public consumption,” and not necessarily realistic, said Daniel Sugaré, the head of family law department at Sugaré & Co. Solicitors in the U.K.

Set in London, “War” tells the story of the shattering end of the decade-long marriage between tech billionaire Morgan Henderson (Dominic West) and his Hollywood star wife, Carla Duval (Sienna Miller), resulting in divorce.
Morgan and Carla hire lawyers from rival London law firms, Cathcarts & Sons and Taylor & Byrne, respectively, to take each other down in court.
Here’s what a real divorce lawyer thinks of the show’s pilot.
Hiring a Lawyer As a Mole? That’s a Big No-No
One of lawyers’ most egregious antics would cause them to lose their law licenses in real life, Sugaré said.
Specifically, Cathcarts & Sons’s move to send struggling young lawyer Johnny Warren (Archie Renaux) to Taylor & Byrne to act as a mole for their case.
“(Johnny) would be struck off immediately by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA),” Sugaré said of the mole.
“You’ve got a duty to your clients to act confidentially, act in their best interests, and by sharing information like in that manner, that they would be bound for disciplinary procedures,” he added.
The higher-ups at Cathcarts & Sons who orchestrated the scheme “would also face significant legal consequences from the SRA and potentially criminal proceedings,” he said.
The bad behavior of the lawyers on the show veers far from what real-life attorneys aim to do: help clients remain calm and focused so they can come to an agreement.
“In certain cases, you have to act in an aggressive way to protect your client’s interest,” said Sugaré. “But in the show, it seems like they’re doing that more than what is necessary.”
Carla’s Cheating Scheme

The show starts with Morgan sleeping with a young woman named Flora (Rose Williams). Turns out the moment has been orchestrated by Carla. She wants to prove that Morgan is unfaithful, and in doing so, exploit the prenuptial’s infidelity clause.
But will Carla’s scheme actually work? Not so fast, Sugaré said.
“An affair is not ordinarily a legal escape route from a prenuptial agreement,” Sugaré said.
Sugaré said infidelity clauses are “unusual” in England, as prenups generally deal with financial agreements rather than penalties for cheating.

“Even if this agreement contains an infidelity clause, Carla could not assume that the court would enforce it. While these cases are fact specific, proof of an affair would not ordinarily invalidate the agreement or entitle her to a larger settlement,” he said.
Serving Papers on the Red Carpet
Morgan and Carla race to be the one to serve the other with divorce papers. Morgan ultimately Carla divorce papers on a red carpet.
It’s a biting and humiliating moment, but not necessarily a tactic that gives Morgan an edge, according to Sugaré.
“The race to start divorce proceedings makes good television, but being the applicant does not give Morgan priority over the assets or make the judge more sympathetic to him,” Sugaré said.
And while serving a divorce application on a red carpet is “legally permissible,” it’s normally facilitated via email, Sugaré says.
So, Is Divorce Really ‘War’?
As for the show’s title? Sugaré said war is an apt metaphor for the potential brutality of divorce.
“It can get aggressive. It can be vicious. It can be personal, and the job of the lawyer is to try and rein your client in,” Sugaré said.

He explained a good lawyer tries to help clients stop ruminating about their emotions and the end of the marriage and instead prepare to “reach sensible agreements or make big decisions about (their) future,” he said.
His advice for anyone entering into a marriage? At the risk of sounding like an “anti-love guy,” Sugaré suggests both parties sign a prenuptial agreement.

“In the right circumstances, a prenuptial agreement can give both parties clarity and certainty. It may not be the most romantic conversation before a wedding, but being open about finances at the outset can prevent far greater conflict later.”

title: 4 Biggest Takeaways From Michael Douglas’ Explosive Memoir
summary: Actor Michael Douglas, who cemented his legendary status after a decadeslong career in Hollywood,” reflects on his wildly eventful life in new memoir “One Helluva Ride.”
story: Actor Michael Douglas, who cemented his legendary status after a decadeslong career in Hollywood,” reflects on his wildly eventful life in new memoir “One Helluva Ride.” And that includes some pretty explosive confessions.

Douglas, best known for his roles in blockbuster films “Wall Street” and “Basic Instinct,” details his personal sagas involving everything from infidelity to struggles with parenting in what many readers have already considered a bombshell of a book.

Now 82, the actor writes that he is refusing to shy away from any aspect of his life, and that includes some of the more unsavory elements, acknowledging that he spent a large part of his career portraying the “modern, flawed, American male.” And that archetype, he adds, “wasn’t exactly a stretch for me.”

With eight decades of drama — literally and figuratively — to unpack, Douglas says in the sprawling, 500-page memoir released Oct. 6, that the account reveals “who I became and the choices I made along the way.”
“I’ve lived a large part of my life in the public eye, but I’m a very private person,” Douglas writes. “Fame can blur the truth. Now it’s time to finally bring it all back into focus.”
Here are some of the most eye-opening highlights from “One Helluva Ride.”
He Had a Complicated Relationship With His Father, Screen Legend Kirk Douglas
Michael Douglas had a complicated, sometimes tenuous relationship with his father Kirk Douglas. And it was one that ended up shaping much of his professional and personal life, he wrote.

Kirk Douglas, who was born Issur Danielovitch Demsky, was the child of Russian Jewish immigrants and had spent much of his upbringing enduring poverty and domestic violence, the memoir says. Aspects of his difficult beginnings bled into the way in which Kirk Douglas parented — a role that, the younger Douglas wrote, involved violence and rage that at times were rationalized as “care.”

But against a backdrop of family tensions were also professional pressures, Michael Douglas wrote. In the book he recounted the way in which he’d struggled to make a name for himself, independent of his father, often having to contend with inevitable comparisons between the two. It was difficult, Michael Douglas wrote, as someone whose Hollywood dad had become synonymous with an iconic gladiator hero.
“I should have been born Mikhail Danielovitch, grandson of a ragman,” he wrote in the memoir. “Instead, I was born Michael Kirk Douglas, son of Spartacus.”

They also experienced some frictions in the field, made all the more complicated by their family dynamic. In one standout experience, Michael Douglas recounted working on “One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest” as a producer and having to reject his own father for the lead role of Randle Patrick “Mac” McMurphy, a character that Kirk Douglas had already portrayed on Broadway. The studio head and director of the project felt that Kirk Douglas was too old for the role, so it went to Jack Nicholson, whose performance would land him an Oscar.

“I saw a flash of my father’s rage, then he was silent. Just as I’d feared, Dad blamed me. He said I had betrayed him. I was crushed,” Michael Douglas wrote, adding that the incident put “a distance between us that would take years to overcome.”

While the father-son duo had their ups and downs throughout the decades, it was a 1991 mid-air helicopter crash that left two dead and Kirk Douglas severely injured that kicked off a strong transformation in the pair’s relationship, Michael Douglas wrote.

“It dramatically changed him — from an actor desperate to find his next role, into a more reflective person who embraced his Jewish roots, his family, and his legacy,” Michael Douglas wrote. “All of us in the family knew he had become a much better man after being given his second chance.”
He Had An Affair With Co-Star Kathleen Turner That He Kept Under Wraps For 40 Years

Among the most shocking revelations in the memoir is the truth behind his long suspected, but never confirmed, affair with co-star Kathleen Turner, with whom he starred in 1984 film “Romancing the Stone.” At the time, Michael Douglas was married to producer Diandra Luker, but wrote that the two were separated.
Though for decades, he and Turner maintained to the public that their on-screen chemistry was just that. Douglas wrote in the memoir that they’d been stretching the truth the whole time.
“It was a lie meant to protect my wife and son, a lie we told the world for 40 years,” Douglas said.

Douglas wrote in the memoir that the pair did indeed fall for each another during production, building a close relationship as they navigated the pressures of the film along with their mutual attraction while shooting in Mexico.

“Following an exhausting day of shooting in the jungle, we’d go out and have a meal, or head out with the group and afterward I would sneak into her hotel room after everybody was asleep,” Douglas said, before referencing their characters. “There were no cameras in elevators, no assistants using cell phones to take pictures. As Jack and Joan were falling in love, Kathleen and I were keeping the chemistry alive.”
Things took a turn, Douglas wrote, when Luker brought their son Cameron Douglas to visit. He recounted that Luker was growing suspicious.

“At some point, she was alone with Kathleen and made it clear to her that we were still married,” he wrote. “Her view of the terms of our separation was different from mine. This gave Kathleen pause. She didn’t want to interfere.”

He wrote that after the visit, he and Turner ended their affair and he went back to Luker. The decision, he explained, was made with his son in mind. Michael Douglas himself was a child of divorce and had been deeply impacted by his parents’ separation, he wrote. But the choice to stay with Luker “may have done more harm than good,” he wrote.
“Even if you are the child of divorce, you still forget that all your kid wants is a peaceful, happy home, and sometimes the best way to do that is to give your kid two homes,” he wrote.

Douglas’ book also mentions other affairs including a brief fling with “Romancing the Stone” screenwriter Diane Thomas and another extramarital relationship with Jeanne Tripplehorn, his co-star in the 1992 film “Basic Instinct,” for whom he was “ready to officially leave my wife.”
He Had to Break Things Off With Five Different Women Before Dating Now-Wife Catherine Zeta-Jones
Catherine Zeta-Jones would become Douglas’ great love in life, however the two had a rather unusual start.

Zeta-Jones was long aware of Douglas’ playboy reputation and made that clear the very first night they met, he said. But he was intent on playing the long game with the actor, who was 25 years his junior.

After months of wooing her — and one pivotal visit to Mallorca, Spain — Douglas finally won over Zeta-Jones. But before they could officially get serious, she laid down the law, telling him that he’d need to commit to a monogamous relationship with her in order for things to work out, Douglas wrote.
“I told her, ‘Wait here, I have to make five quick calls,’” Douglas recounted.
Douglas explained that after his separation from his wife, he began seeing five different women who all lived in different cities.
“That day, I called each one to say I’d met somebody and would no longer be able to continue seeing them,” Douglas wrote. “They all took it well.”

Douglas described his relationship with Zeta-Jones as different from any others he’s ever had. And even amid their brief separation in 2013, precipitated by Douglas’ tongue cancer and Zeta-Jones’s bipolar diagnosis, he wrote that he “never gave hope that we would reconcile.”
“I love Catherine in a way that I have never loved any other woman,” he wrote. “She’s my wife, my best friend, and my life partner. I could never lose her.”
He and Rob Reiner Bonded Over Having Sons Who Were Battling Addiction Issues

Michael Douglas and the late director and actor Rob Reiner had a friendship that spanned more than 50 years. Among their many similarities — which also included having famous dads (Rob Reiner being comedy legend Carl Reiner’s son) — was their difficult relationships with their sons who were contending with serious drug issues.

In the memoir, Douglas recounted his son’s struggles with drugs and the 2009 federal case that got Cameron Douglas sentenced to five years in prison. Cameron Douglas, who was arrested for possession of crystal meth, would end up serving nearly eight years for drug trafficking charges and drug possession while in prison.

Reiner’s son Nick Reiner had also struggled with substance abuse issues, attending a number of rehab programs between ages 15 to 19. Rob Reiner, 78, and his wife Michele Singer Reiner, 70, were found dead in their Brentwood, California, home in Dec. 2025. Nick Reiner has since been charged with murder.

“We both had sons with serious drug issues and we both, at times, had been at the end of our rope. It was a heartbreaking confessional for us, but I know we gave each other some measure of comfort during the hard times,” Douglas wrote.
Douglas remembered his late friend with some moving words.
“Rob and his lovely wife Michele were extraordinarily kind, fundamentally decent, loving people who wanted a better tomorrow for everyone,” he wrote.

title: ‘Crazy Rich Asians’ Is Officially Getting a Sequel In the Form of a TV Show
summary: Almost 10 years after its release, “Crazy Rich Asians” is officially getting a sequel — sort of.
story: Almost 10 years after its release, “Crazy Rich Asians” is officially getting a sequel — sort of.

On Oct. 8, HBO announced that they have greenlit an eight episode series that will pick up after the events of the 2018 film. Along with the news, they also confirmed that Constance Wu, Henry Golding, Ronny Chieng and Michelle Yeoh would be reprising their roles.

The one-hour drama series is based on Kevin Kwan’s book series. Adele Lim, who co-wrote the film, will showrun and executive produce the show alongside Kwan, Nina Jacobson, Brad Simpson, and the film’s director Jon M. Chu.
In a teaser, HBO shared that production for the series will start in 2027.

“I am thrilled that the ‘Crazy Rich Asians’ family is getting back together,” Kwan said in a statement, thanking HBO and Warner Bros. Television. “Our incredible fans around the world have been patiently waiting for this, and it will be worth the wait! Getting to see my stories and characters come to life with the breathing room of an HBO series is a dream come true, and I am so excited to experience the magic that Adele, Jon, Nina, Brad, our amazing writers and iconic cast will create.”
Chu, who most recently directed the “Wicked” films, added that, eight years ago, “Crazy Rich Asians” changed his life.

“I got to make it with the most creative and hilarious group of people I’ve ever known. Since then, this cast has become movie stars, superheroes, arena-filling performers and even an Oscar winner,” the filmmaker continued, adding that bringing everyone back together “feels like coming home.”
He noted that it has been incredible watching people make this movie part of their lives, “from mahjong nights to becoming the ultimate airplane movie.”
Chu said that he’s excited to finally get the chance to answer the question he’s been asked almost every day for eight years: “‘When are we getting the sequel?’ Well… bok bok b-----, we’re back.”

“Crazy Rich Asians” follows humble professor Rachel Chu (Wu) as she travels with her boyfriend Nick Young (Golding) to Singapore, where she discovers that he is rich — like, filthy rich. As she’s thrust into a world with some of the wealthiest and most influential families in the country, she faces rejection from Nick’s mother, Eleanor (Yeoh).
The rom-com also starred Awkwafina, Gemma Chan, Ken Jeong and a brief appearance by Harry Shum Jr.
After its release, “Crazy Rich Asians” became the highest-grossing Hollywood studio romantic comedy at the North American box office in nearly a decade.

title: Who Was Banished and Who Was Murdered in ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Episode 5?
summary: A banishment and murder took place on the Oct. 8 episode of “The Traitors: New Blood.” Read what happened.
story: Warning: Spoilers from “The Traitors: New Blood” Episode 5 below.
Murder and mayhem are keeping the all-civilian cast of “The Traitors: New Blood” on their toes.

The bloodbath continued Oct. 8 in Episode 5, titled “Wake of the Living Dead” when viewers learned Katie’s fate after the  cliffhanger moment from the show’s last episode when Jay revealed at the Round Table he suspected Katie was a Traitor.
Viewers at home, of course, knew Jay was right about Katie, who was invited to be an accomplice by the season’s original Traitor duo Joe and Tomica.
Tensions at the Round Table
As Jay shared more about his suspicions, Katie derailed him by revealing to the group Jay previously told her Kriste was a Traitor.
Already on thin ice with the group because of his chaotic behavior, Jay told Kriste, “I don’t know 100% if you’re a Traitor,” explaining he was suspicious of her because she avoided his eye contact.
Exasperated, Kriste told Jay in her Mississippi drawl she avoided looking at him because she’d become, like others in the castle, tired of his incessant chatter.
“Listening to your theories and your information is about as informative and as interesting as picking gnat crap out of pepper,” Kriste said.
As Jay tried to explain himself, Katie, eager to change the subject, cut him off, saying, “Let’s move on.”

Next, Abby L. said a conversation she’d had with Sherry provided her with all the “evidence” she needed that Sherry was a Traitor. Abby L. recalled Sherry telling her, “There’s no way all three of the Traitors are women.”
“How do you know that for sure there are three Traitors?” Abby L. recalled thinking, which made her believe Sherry was in on the villainy.
Sherry, showing off a previously unseen fiery side, defended herself by saying others in the group had also thrown out guesses about the number of Traitors among them.
Sherry then revealed she suspected Jay.
“Your behavior during this whole game has been more treacherous than any Traitor,” Sherry told Jay. “You seem to delight in creating a crockpot of confusion that we all simmer in.”
Everyone in the castle judged Jay for his refusal to sacrifice himself for his team during missions, Sherry said, adding, “You are a detriment to all of us playing this game.”
The Banishment
When the time came for banishment, Sherry received the most votes, including one from Jay, despite the fact that he’d just voiced his suspicions about Katie and Kriste.
Before exiting, Sherry shocked the others by revealing she was a Faithful, making her the third Faithful in a row the group unwittingly sent home.
“Do better,” Sherry icily told the remaining players.
Host Alan Cumming then mocked the group for their banishment selections. “Faithfuls, once again you have voted out one of your own,” he told them.
A Traitor Gets Tearful

After the banishment, a tearful Katie privately told Joe their Traitorous lies and manipulations were taking a toll on her. “I feel horrible. I kind of want to go cry. I don’t really want to do it anymore,” Katie said.
“It’s hard,” Joe replied, reminding her it was all just a game.
“They’re just never going to forgive us,” Katie said.
In a confessional, a sobbing Katie said she was “struggling” being a villain.
“I don’t want to see any of these people go. I forget whose side I’m on,” Katie said. “I genuinely get so immersed in my conversations, I forget that I’m the problem.”
A Murder in Plain Sight
Later, all three Traitors received notes informing them their next task was to commit a murder in plain sight before the players attended a staged funeral later that night.

The Traitors were instructed to locate a bunch of “cursed apples” in the castle’s kitchen and to then toss an apple to one of the nine remaining players. Whoever caught the tossed apple would later be revealed as the murder victim.
Joe took an apple to a room where Jay, Morgan, Mark, Clyde and Tomica sat on a sofa. He tossed the apple to Morgan, but she failed to catch it.
Victor later became suspicious after Tomica offered him an apple and seeing Joe walking around the castle with a second apple in his hand.
“No shade. I haven’t seen Joe eat a lot of fruit the last couple days,” Victor said in a confessional.
A Wake for the Living Dead
The players, all dressed in black, joined Alan at the outdoor funeral, which took place in a graveyard filled with tombstones with the players’ names.
“Welcome to the Wake of the Living Dead,” Alan announced.
Alan then told seven players — Katie, Abbey B., Jay, Shane, Michael, Ben and Wyatt — they were safe for the night.
The nine remaining players — Tomica, Kriste, Abby L., Morgan, Victor, Clyde, Mark, Joe and Niyyah were placed in coffins and buried in the ground.
Ever so slowly, Alan began revealing which of the buried “poor souls” had escaped death, while also confirming that a murder in plain sight had taken place that night.
One by one, Tomica, Kriste, Abby L., Morgan and Victor were pulled from their coffins, leaving Clyde, Mark, Joe and Niyyah in the ground.
Who among the remaining four were safe and who was going home?
“I can reveal that the Traitors have murdered...” Alan said as the episode faded to black.
What Will Happen Next Week?
Learn the identity of the victim of the murder in plain sight when Episode 6 of “The Traitors: New Blood,” titled “A Murder of Necessity,” arrives Thursday, Oct. 15 at 8 p.m. ET/ PT on NBC.

title: ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Pros Valentin Chmerkovskiy and Jenna Johnson Lead Season 35. But Are They Competitive?
summary: “Dancing With the Stars” Valentin Chmerkovskiy and Jenna Johnson discuss their work, life balance, if they’re competitive with each other and more.
story: Amid their busy lives on and off the ballroom floor, Jenna Johnson and Valentin Chmerkovskiy look for small moments in their everyday life that make them feel at home.
The “Dancing With the Stars” pros and real-life husband and wife are currently competing on Season 35, with Johnson partnered with Harry Shum Jr. and Chmerkovskiy with Jenna Dewan.

Paired with trained dancers, they have often been at the top of the leaderboard since the new “DWTS” season premiered mid-September. In the Oct 6 episode, during Mariah Carey Night, the couples received the same scores, tying for second place.
So how competitive are they with each other?

“I’ve never been competitive with Jenna. I’m only passionate about creating, only passionate about my art or my work or the effort that I put into ‘Dancing With the Stars,’” Chmerkovskiy, 40, tells TODAY.com. “So, it’s not a competition of, can I do it better than her? The competition is, can I produce my best work? And I think both of us can do that. I could support her and be ‘competitive’ at the same time.”
When they aren’t creating choreography or rehearsing with their celebrities, they enjoy quality time with their 3-year-old son Rome. Their time together, they say, makes life more “fabulous.”

“I think we forget that we live a very high-intensity life, and we get to experience so many glamorous things,” Johnson, 32, tells TODAY.com, while chatting about their “Make Your World More Fabuloso” campaign. “Like, I dress up for a living, that’s my job. But I really think that the fabulous parts of my life are being with my son and my husband at home. Those are the moments that I cherish. That’s what a luxurious life for me looks like.”
“We’re obviously in a really unique situation and period of our life, but those moments are so fabulous for me,” she adds.
The couple, who recently became homeowners, embrace finding new ways to make routines, even household chores, more enjoyable.

“Your home is your domain. It’s your haven. It’s your sanctuary, and the way it smells, the effort that it takes to clean together as a family and making it fun, these are things that we connect on,” Chmerkovskiy says.
They also connect on how they decompress post shows. After a grueling week on “DWTS” and surviving another elimination, the couple likes to “debrief” and go out to dinner.

“Not many people work with their spouse and also in a public setting where we are publicly perceived. It is crazy and there’s no real blueprint on it,” Johnson says. “I am really proud of our relationship and the work that Val and I have done (together).”
When it comes to maintaining a healthy work, life balance, she credits these three things: communication, trust and prioritizing each other.

“I think people are like, ‘Oh, you’re so lucky. You get to work together. You see each other all the time.’ But we’re at work. That’s us being on set,” she adds. “We’re both so passionate about what we do, so we have blinders on. We’re really focused on our partners and on our dance and making it the best it can be.”
Competitive or not, a healthy balance, they say, is making sure they have date nights, “Where we just sit down, debrief and talk and see how each other are doing.”
Of course, time with their son “brings us the most joy and happiness.”

“It definitely is a balancing act. But I am proud of how we’ve navigated it because it’s crazy working with your significant other,” Johnson says. “Throughout the chaos of our lives, we love those consistent things that make us feel like home, calm our nerves down and relax.”

title: Serena Williams Reveals Her 2nd Barbie Collab of the Year, and What it Means to Her Daughters
summary: TODAY has the exclusive reveal of the second Barbie doll created in the likeness of Serena Williams, including an interview with the tennis pro herself.
story: Serena Williams, one of the greatest athletes of all time, is more than worthy of having a doll designed in her image. So Barbie gave her two.

After Mattel released a Williams Barbie earlier this year in honor of International Women’s Day that highlighted her entrepreneurial side since “evolving away from tennis,” the company partnered with her again to design another doll that celebrates her legacy on the court.

The latest Barbie Signature Serena Williams Doll, arriving just in time for International Day of the Girl, sports the same kit the icon wore at the 2005 Australian Open when she defeated Lindsay Davenport. Her Barbie wears a lime green and white cutout mesh top, with a white skirt and matching socks and sweatband. She holds a tennis racket and ball in her hands, of course.
TODAY independently determines what we cover and recommend. When you click on or buy through our links, we earn a commission.
Barbie Signature Serena Williams Doll

“It’s something that was memorable that I can play with with my girls, like the other one. So it’s like two sides of me. It’s like the business side and the sports side,” she tells TODAY.com about her two collaborations with Mattel and Barbie. (The new one-of-a-kind doll will be available for purchase at Target and online mass retails beginning Oct. 8.)

While Williams donned many unforgettable fits in her 23-grand slam victories, she says her 2005 design and win hold a special significance for her, which is why she wanted to further immortalize that title.

“That slam meant so much to me. I was able to come back from so many downs, and even in the finals of that match, I was down so much,” she recalls about the 2–6, 6–3, 6–0 battle. “But I was somehow able to never give up. So when I’m playing with my daughters, I always want (to teach) them to never give up.”

She continues, “When we were thinking of different outfits, we kept going back and forth, and that one just kept standing out. The colors were really fantastic on it, as well. We thought that that also told a really good story.”
Daughters Olympia, 9, and Adira, 3, whom she shares with husband Alexis Ohanian, have been busy playing with both Barbies.
“We were just playing with the sport one yesterday, so they like anything new,” she says laughing. Her daughters have also been putting the mini version of their mom’s 2005 look on their other dolls.
Williams adds, “My doll is the mom doll, so it’s kind of funny.”

The proud mom has shared that her daughters inspired her return to professional tennis a few months ago, one of the biggest sports stories this year. Williams’ first match since the 2022 US Open came at the Queen’s Club in June when she played doubles alongside Canada’s Victoria Mboko. She has since played doubles in Berlin with Czech’s Karolína Muchová, singles at Wimbledon and Cincinnati doubles with sister Venus Williams. Most recently, she competed at the 2026 US Open in doubles with her sister and mixed doubles with Carlos Alcaraz.
Williams previously said she wanted Olympia and Adira to see her play which helped fuel her comeback. Both have been spotted in the stands supporting their mom.

Her oldest daughter is “pumped up” just to see her playing professionally, Williams shares. As for her youngest, she thinks every match her mom plays is a win. Both also attend practices to watch their mom train.
“For my daughters, (it) doesn’t matter whether I win or lose. They’re just excited to be there,” she explains. “They love it, and I love it.”
Williams says it has been “very manageable” navigating being a mom of two and competing again. She also shares if tennis fans can expect to see her on the court again soon.

“My main career is investing, so my tennis career is so little. I’m not playing anymore this year,” she reveals. “If I play next year, it’ll be so very few tournaments. Because I am a full-time mom, and that’s my main goal. That’s what I want to do with them right now. Nothing trumps being with them.”
Williams says she had always planned to only play a few times this year following her return.

“I have another job that I take extremely seriously,” says Williams, who recently rebranded her firm from Serena Ventures to Starfire Ventures. “I can’t play too much. But, it’s also fun that I’m able to play a little bit.”
She points out that working to secure a deal gives her a similar feeling she felt when seeing her opponent on the other side of the net.
“When it comes to competition, I still have what I need, just not as much with the travel,” she says. “But this is different. This is playing for different stakes, and it’s very stressful.”
While investing will be her main focus as the year winds down, fans might still see Williams on the court from time to time.
“I always hit, even if I’m not playing professional tennis. I use it as a way to stay fit,” she shares.
As for whether she’ll ramp up training for another tournament, she adds, “We’ll see how it goes.”

title: Carson Daly Gets Emotional After Hearing Wynonna Judd’s New Song: ‘Every Lyric Hits Home’
summary: Carson Daly said Wynonna Judd’s song “Girl Who Could Sing,” reminded him of his own father, who died when he was a boy.
story: Wynonna Judd performed a new song, “Girl Who Could Sing,” Oct. 8 on TODAY, and it certainly resonated with Carson Daly.
The track, from her first new album in 10 years, “The Hard Truth,” is about how she never met her biological father.
“I didn’t find out he was my real father until I was 30. So this is a very heavy song,” she said before playing it.
After wrapping up, Carson was visibly moved.
“Wow, you’re getting me there, man,” he said.
“My goodness,” she said.
“Yeah, I didn’t know my biological father, so that song, like every lyric of that hits home,” he said.
Carson’s biological father, Jim Daly, died of bladder cancer in 1979 when Carson was 5.
During the pandemic in 2020, he and his older sister, Quinn, re-created a photo of him mixing a drink in the 1970s while wearing a UCLA zip-up.
“I feel like I time traveled back to like 1978 for a second there and entered the personal space of my father, and I’m grateful for that,” Carson said on TODAY at the time.
“I have so few shared experiences with him, it’s like a powerful moment,” he said.
For Carson, the performance and song’s premise struck a chord.

“For me it was just cool putting on the UCLA sweatshirt because I have so few things that connect me to my biological father,’’ he said. “To be able to re-create that photo was really cool. That dichotomy I see in Dad’s face when I look at that picture. I don’t know if he’s running from fear or head into it.”

A few years after his father died, Carson’s mother, Patti, married Richard Caruso, whom Carson called “Pops.” The couple died five weeks apart in 2017 from unrelated ailments. Carson had a strong relationship with Caruso and mourned his death.
“Pops passed away today with absolute dignity & pride. The greatest man we ever knew. Our hero,” he wrote on Instagram.

“He exemplified great faith, loyalty to family & hard work. He provided us all with so much. We’re grateful. His legacy lives on in all of us & anyone who had the pleasure of meeting him. He’s reunited with mom now.”

Judd has opened up about how the man she believed to be her father, Michael Ciminella, was not actually her dad. Her biological father was man named Charles Jordan. He dated her mother, Naomi, when they were teenagers.

“She was very much in love with him, and they were just too young ... she got pregnant, and that’s that,” Judd told People last month. “Back in 1963 that just didn’t happen without there being consequences that were intense.”
It was a development she addressed in “Girl Who Could Sing.”
“I was 30 years old when I learned the truth, that the man I called ‘Dad’ my entire life, was not my biological father,” she said in a statement released along with the song.

“It changed everything I thought I knew about who I was. By the time I was ready to meet him, he was gone. I never got to hear his voice, look him in the eyes, or ask him why. I’ll carry those unanswered questions with me for the rest of my life. ‘Was I ever really your daughter, or just a girl who could sing?’ is the question that hurts the most — because I’ll never get to hear his answer. What do you do with the questions you’ll never have answers to? My answer is simple … I sing about it.”

title: Catherine Zeta-Jones Shares Why She Has Yet to Read Husband Michael Douglas’ Memoir
summary: Catherine Zeta-Jones admits she hasn’t finished her husband Michael Douglas’ memoir “One Helluva Ride” for this reason.
story: As Hollywood fans buzz about the revelations in legendary actor Michael Douglas’ memoir, there is still one reviewer working on getting around to reading it — his wife.
Actor Catherine Zeta-Jones, who has been married to Douglas for almost 26 years, told Willie Geist on TODAY Oct. 8 that she hasn’t yet made time to pick up “One Helluva Ride,” which published Oct. 6.
Between filming Season 3 of the Netflix hit “Wednesday” and the new AMC+ series “Kill Jackie,” there hasn’t been much time for reading after long days at work, she said.

“I just finished ‘Wednesday,’ Season 3, we shot in Dublin for seven months, and then I just literally got on a Ryanair plane and landed in London, did all of the ‘Kill Jackie’ stuff. Then I went to Bilbao, Spain, and now I’m here talking to you, Will, on the fabulous TODAY show.
“And as much as I love my husband, when I’m tired at night, I have no intention of reading about him. At all,” she added.

While she hasn’t gotten to it yet, she said “everyone else should” take in the Hollywood tale of the 82-year-old actor, known for indelible roles in everything from “Basic Instinct” to “Wall Street” and growing up the son of actor Kirk Douglas.
“The book is called ‘One Helluva Ride,’ and I think everyone should hold on to their cowboy hats because I think it is,” she said.
Zeta-Jones, 57, gets her own chapter in the book, appropriately titled “Catherine.” Douglas describes seeing the Welsh actor for the first time in the 1998 movie “The Mask of Zorro.”
“I had never fallen in love with a woman on a movie screen before,” he writes. “Until I saw Catherine.”
He read in an interview that she liked older men. Douglas and Zeta-Jones, who share a birthday, are exactly 25 years apart in age.
“I said to myself, ‘Hey I’ve got a shot!’” he writes.
The two first met while they were promoting separate movies at a film festival in France.
“She was smart, funny, unpretentious, and yes, breathtakingly beautiful,” Douglas writes.
However, he nearly botched it when he met up with Jones, got “smashed” at the bar after she left, then saw her again that night and blurted out, “I’m going to be the father of your children.”
Douglas was able to smooth it over with a massive delivery of flowers. Plus, he wasn’t wrong. The two now share son Dylan, 26, and daughter Carys, 23.
“I was certain, as much as I had ever been about anything, that she was the one,” Douglas writes.

Zeta-Jones wanted to be exclusive with him when they were first together, and he told her he had to “make five quick calls.” He writes that he was dating five different women at the time while also finalizing a divorce from his first wife, Diandra Luker.
The two first appeared as a couple at the premiere of the 1999 Zeta-Jones and Sean Connery hit “Entrapment.” They got married in 2000, three months after Dylan Douglas was born.
“We have an intense love for each other, a great need for each other and a great respect for each other,” Douglas writes.

title: Before AI, There Was Hero 1, The Personal Robot Who Visited TODAY in 1982
summary: A robot named Hero 1 visited TODAY in 1982, while its creator explained how it worked and what it could do.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights a custom-made robot that stopped by the show on Dec. 1, 1982.

In an era when the debate around AI continues to grow louder, it’s an interesting time to look back and see a technological advance from decades ago that may have signaled what robots and AI could do.
On Dec. 1, 1982, TODAY’s Nancy Foreman sat down with a custom-made personal robot called Hero 1.

“Meet Hero 1, the first mass produced domestic robot. It has an onboard computer, a sonar device. It talks, listens, moves about on three wheels, has (a) movable arm,” she said while also introducing the man who controlled it, Jim Lytle, its chief engineer and production line manager for Heathkit Educational Products.
Lytle said Hero 1 was in development for three years.
How Did Hero 1 Function?
The robot, which looks like a mashup of R2-D2, a copy machine and a vacuum, could count and tell time, but that was just the tip of the iceberg.
“Like all computer-controlled devices, ultimately he responds only to those programs or commands that are put in by the programmer,” Lytle said before typing in some instructions.
The robot then talked in a stereotypical monotone voice so associated with robots.
“I have a brain, just like you do, but my brain is a computer,” it said.
“I always do as I am programmed,” it added.
How Does It Know to Talk and Do Tasks?

“The system we use here uses the basic sounds that make up the English language to synthesize words. It has an unlimited vocabulary,” Lytle said, while noting Hero 1 weighed about 40 pounds and could go roughly an hour without being recharged.
Lytle was also armed with a teaching pendant, which looked like a remote control.

“This permits me to actually manually control the movements of the robot, but it’s more than just a remote control,” he said, “because as I do this, the robot is remembering all the motions that I’ve entered into the memory, and then on command he can repeat these, precisely and in the exact sequence that I’ve taught him,” he said.
What Kind of Tasks Could Hero 1 Do?
While Hero 1 could do a variety of things, Lytle said it was “designed primarily as a training device.
“However, there are a lot of practical applications that he could be put to in the home, using the various sensors that he has,” he added.
Lytle confirmed Schulman’s guess that the robot couldn’t operate stairs, though.
“I’m thinking maybe he could get the paper in the morning,” Schulman said.
“Oh, he could do that as long as he didn’t have to, as you say, negotiate the stairs,” Lytle replied.
Hero 1 cost $1,500 as a kit that consumers had to put together on their own, while the factory-assembled version cost $2,500.
Was Hero 1 a Sign of Things to Come?
Schulman asked if the robot would be the “grandfather of future robots.”
“To teach the consumer, and eventually it can interface with other appliances and really do some work around the house, right?” Schulman asked.
“Very possibly, yes,” Lytle said. “The technology is here today to do these things. It’s just a matter of somebody making the commitment, and we’re putting our foot in the door.”

title: Our 1 Big Question for Kat Cunning During Commercial: Is the ‘Line of Fire’ Cast Close in Real Life?
summary: Line of Fire star Kat Cunning talks about the new show, her character’s relationship to her siblings and parents, the actors’ real bonds and more.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.
“Line of Fire” is proving as much a law enforcement procedural as it is a twisty family drama.

In NBC’s new Monday night show, Kat Cunning stars as FBI agent Clare Hollingsworth, the eldest daughter in a family of protective service agents. Dad Mike (Peter Krause) and middle son Micah (Tommy O’Brien) work in Secret Service. Youngest brother Russ (Taylor Bloom) is an analyst at the Department of Justice. And mom Jane (Hope Davis) is a U.S. Marshal, meaning she and Clare consistently run into each other on the job, turning personal squabbles into a power struggle over jurisdiction.

Only three episodes into Season 1, Clare has been through a lot. She was strong-armed into bringing her new boyfriend to a family dinner — only for that boyfriend to get shot by his seemingly friendly neighbor, who, surprise, is none other than Clare’s “dead” older half-brother, Jack (Charlie Barnett).

When she soldiers on through her grief, she winds up held up at gunpoint after an investigation goes wrong. Oh, and her departed sweet, schoolteacher boyfriend? He was actually a CIA operative, and Clare was the assignment.

But as twisty as the plot gets, it’s the simpler moments, like Russ setting up appointments for Clare to see a grief counselor, or the siblings sitting together on park swings together after a family dinner implodes, that grounds the show.
According to Cunning, it’s attributable to a cast chemistry that “you can’t fake.”

TODAY.com caught up with Cunning in Studio 1A’s Orange Room to discuss that twist with Jack, unpack the secret sauce to their family dynamic and preview what’s ahead for the rest of “Line of Fire” Season 1.

title: Valerie Bertinelli Defends Tribute To Eddie Van Halen: ‘I Love Ed. Never Stopped Loving Ed’
summary: Actor Valerie Bertinelli is defending herself against online haters who criticized her recent tribute to her late ex-husband, Eddie Van Halen.
story: Actor Valerie Bertinelli is defending herself against online haters who criticized her recent tribute to her late ex-husband, Eddie Van Halen.

Bertinelli doubled down on her recent Instagram post in honor of the sixth anniversary of the rock icon’s death Oct. 6. The tribute post prompted some fans to accuse her of holding on to the old relationship. But in a new video shared Oct. 7, Bertinelli told her critics that “you can’t bother me.”
“I love Ed. Never stopped loving Ed. And my heart loves a lot,” she said in the clip. “Don’t you wish yours could too?”
Bertinelli’s throwback photo featured the one-time couple, sharing a laugh in a car.
“Photos may fade, like old photos do, but not the memories and never the love,” the 66-year-old wrote in the post’s caption.

The former “One Day at a Time” and “Hot in Cleveland” star was married to Van Halen from 1981 until 2007. She filed for divorce in 2005 after being separated for several years. The musician went on to marry Janie Liszewski in 2009, with whom he remained married until his death. Meanwhile, Bertinelli married financial planner Tom Vitale in 2011. They divorced in 2022.

Bertinelli, who shares a son with the rocker, musician Wolfgang Van Halen, 35, hit back at the criticisms in the new video that was captioned, “Strap in haters, let’s go for a little ride.” She told fans that she gets “pushback” any time she posts about her late ex.

Bertinelli, who remained close with Eddie Van Halen after their divorce — and was at the rocker’s bedside when he died in 2020 after a 20-year battle with cancer—  said often critics tell her she’s “not allowed to love” her former husband.
Those critics, she said, “berate you and berate you for months, make you think you’re crazy, until you finally say, ‘OK, fine, I don’t love him.’”
The scorn has caused her to remove images of  the late music legend from her account, Bertinelli said.

“They will never say, ‘Take that picture down, the one of your ex-husband along with you and your son in better days,’” she shared. “But they say that you’re obsessed, say all kinds of f----- up s--- until you take the picture down,” she said.
Bertinelli revealed that the musician, whom she began dating when she was 20, still holds a “big piece” of her heart.

“If I ever fall in love again, I’ll make room in my heart for that person, without it touching the love I have for Ed, my son, my daughter-in-law, all the people that I love,” she said. “Your heart opens up. Because your heart can hold a lot of love. All of our hearts can.”

title: Her Home Burned. Her Late Husband’s Basketball Hoop Didn’t. Now She’s Building Again
summary: Layla Hawkins is one of the thousands who were displaced by the Pacific Palisades fire that swept through the Los Angeles neighborhood, destroying some 6,800 homes, businesses and structures in one of the largest and most expensive disasters in California history.
story: Layla Hawkins had less than 10 minutes to pack up her cherished belongings before a wildfire on Jan. 7, 2025 took her beloved home of four decades. It left behind only a treasured basketball hoop that belonged to her late husband, Los Angeles sports star Tommy Hawkins, a motivation for the grieving homeowner to rebuild again in his honor.

Layla Hawkins is one of the thousands who were displaced by the Pacific Palisades fire that swept through the Los Angeles neighborhood, destroying some 6,800 homes, businesses and structures in one of the largest and most expensive disasters in California history. The blaze left 12 people dead.

Now, almost two years after the fires, Layla Hawkins is on the road to fulfilling her goal in memory of her late husband, thanks in part to nonprofit Habitat for Humanity, whose volunteers from its ReBUILD LA initiative are helping her pick up the pieces. She tells TODAY.com that she is “forever grateful.”
Hawkins says that seeing people come together to help her is “like having an army of relatives surrounding you and giving you hope, love and generous hugs. That’s priceless.”

The Palisades fire — in addition to the Eaton fire that burned simultaneously on the opposite end of Los Angeles, claiming the lives of 19 people and destroying 9,418 homes and other buildings — was an eye-opening experience for Hawkins. That day, she left her home with her husband’s ashes in hand and dog Shiloh. She says she could feel the heat from the fire.

“I lived in Malibu for 40 years. I had gone through quite a few fires and we have always been ready to go and get everything ready and come back,” Hawkins says. “That day, it was something out of a movie script. We only had about eight minutes to vacate and leave.”
She said she hoped evacuating would be similar to her past experiences in which she’d eventually return to see her home still standing. She wasn’t so lucky.

“I could see the fires viciously going crazy, way out of control. And I said to myself, and I said to my home, ‘I will see you in a few hours, like all the other times. Don’t worry, we’ll be fine,’” she recalls. “And as I stopped for just some reason, out of the blue, I looked back. I (had) a lump in my throat and I just knew that I would never see my home again.”
When she arrived back on her property later on, she hesitated before stepping out of her car, she recalls. Little remained of her home, she says.
However, a moment of optimism filled her heavy heart after she saw a blue starfish bank where she and her husband would share love notes with each other, she adds.
“I looked in that massive destruction, and I saw that little starfish, blue, deep blue, just staring at me,” she says. “I just went over there, and I remember I kneeled, and I said, ‘Tommy.’”

Even more moving, Hawkins says, was the discovery that her husband’s basketball hoop had survived the fire. Tommy Hawkins had a 10-year NBA career and played for the Los Angeles Lakers for six seasons, as well as with the Cincinnati Royals for four. He also worked with the Los Angeles Dodgers as vice president of communications.
“I remember I walked over and I gave it a big hug,” she says. “I hugged it so tight because I was hugging my home. I was hugging Tommy.”
From that moment, she made a promise to her late husband that she would return and rebuild their home.

Rebuilding efforts have been difficult, she says, but she made inroads on that promise after she received an email from Habitat for Humanity, informing her that they would help her reconstruct. She was shocked, she says, and read the email over and over to make sure it was real.

“It took me a few hours to actually settle down and write a letter to them. And from that day on, they have been with me every step,” she says, adding that they’ve helped with paperwork, permits and more.

Most recently, Habitat for Humanity of Greater Los Angeles held a four-day Pacific Palisades Community Build effort, from Sept. 23–26, during which Hawkins saw hundreds of volunteers working on her home as well as that of others. The group’s wall-framing and landscaping efforts, she says, brought a sense of community back to the destroyed land.
“I just (have) this feeling that I’m going to have the biggest Christmas tree up in my home by Christmastime,” she says with a laugh, adding that Habitat’s help has made her smile once again.
The expected completion date for Hawkins’ home is June 2027, pending weather.

title: Deadly Saudi airport strikes mark major Mideast escalation
summary: Fears of intensifying conflict were growing in Saudi Arabia on Monday after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis launched multiple strikes on Riyadh’s airport over the weekend, killing 13 people and wounding hundreds.
story: RIYADH, Saudi Arabia — Fears of intensifying conflict were growing in Saudi Arabia on Monday after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis launched multiple strikes on Riyadh’s airport over the weekend, killing 13 people and wounding hundreds.
“What is clear is we remain on a strong escalation ladder,” said Adam Baron, a fellow at New America, a Washington, D.C.-based think tank, who follows Yemen and the wider Gulf region.

More than 300 people were injured when the kingdom’s main international airport was attacked Saturday, marking a major escalation in the Houthi rebel group’s campaign against the world’s leading oil exporter and key U.S. ally in the region.

Among the victims were one American, as well as four citizens of Saudi Arabia, two Bangladeshi nationals, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Palestinian, a Syrian and one Sudanese national. The Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia later said that an Indian national injured in Saturday’s attack had died.
Video capturing the Saturday attack showed a packed airport before the flash of an explosion sends people running for safety as debris falls on them.
The airport remained shut Monday.
The impact of the attacks were felt at the WPC Energy Congress in the Saudi capital Monday, with several top energy executives dropping off the event’s schedule.

The chief executives of Exxon Mobil, TotalEnergies, Shell, Chevron and BP had all been expected at the event, which started Sunday, but were no longer on the agenda that conference organizers released early Monday, Reuters reported. The energy giants did not immediately respond to requests for comment from NBC News.

“You know this country is safe and that we hold your protection at whole heart,” Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said, according to Reuters, as he opened Monday’s session of the gathering held just miles away from Riyadh airport. But, he added, “our gathering here does not mean the risk is gone.”
He said the stepped-up fighting was serious and that the kingdom’s response must be “equally serious.”
“There is no way that somebody will break our back. We are like a phoenix,” he separately said. “We come out of the ashes all the time and every time.”

Fighting on the ground in neighboring Yemen is also intensifying, with the Houthis expanding their operations along its Red Sea coast and around the Bab el Mandeb, a key shipping route connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.
Saudi Arabia and the Houthis began fighting in 2015 after the kingdom entered Yemen’s civil war on behalf of the internationally recognized government.

A period of relative calm following a 2022 ceasefire was shattered in July when the Houthis resumed attacks after accusing Saudi Arabia of striking Sanaa airport as a plane from Iran was attempting to land.

Baron said the latest attacks — the deadliest by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia in more than a decade — could have a “galvanizing effect” on Washington and other international actors, including Pakistan and Turkey, which recently reached a joint defense agreement with the kingdom.
Saudi Arabia defiant following multiple strikes on Riyadh

“As these attacks are growing stronger and stronger, on the one hand, it’s increasing the hurt on the kingdom, but it’s also increasing assessments for many that there has to be some strong effort to degrade the Houthis and restore deterrence,” Baron said.
Washington faces mounting pressure. President Donald Trump on Saturday said he was still weighing whether to join in Saudi Arabia’s military operations against the Houthis.
“We may. We’re gonna look at it,” he told reporters. “We just found out about the recent attack. So we’ll make a decision. We move very quickly.”

After sweeping gains by Houthi forces in Yemen last month, Trump said the rebel group had contacted the U.S. to stress that it doesn’t “want to fight with us” and would “much prefer not having us involved.”
While the skies over Riyadh were empty Monday after flights in and out of the capital were canceled, roads were full of traffic as residents tried to get back to normal life.
And in the early hours of Sunday, road crossings at the border with the United Arab Emirates were largely deserted.

“With the Houthis, we knew that they could hit Riyadh airport, but it’s almost about the precision,” Baron said. “There’s a great degree of anxiety in terms of ... living in a world where you can just have random armed groups hitting airports.”

title: Trump eases Russia sanctions, says Putin will release diesel as prices spike
summary: President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin would “immediately” release hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel fuel onto the global market.
story: President Donald Trump said Friday that Russian President Vladimir Putin would “immediately” release hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel fuel onto the global market.
Trump made the announcement on Truth Social and said the action would will help bring diesel prices down.

Since its illegal invasion of Ukraine, wide-ranging sanctions have been applied to Russia. In order to get the diesel fuel moved, the Treasury Department simultaneously announced Friday that it would be easing sanctions on Russia through April 7.

“Today, at President Trump’s direction, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is immediately issuing a temporary general license to allow the supply of Russian diesel to the global market,” the Treasury Department said on X.

A document posted to the Treasury’s website said that “the sale, delivery, offloading, or importation, including importation into the United States, of diesel fuel of Russian Federation origin are authorized through 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time, April 7, 2027.

In a separate statement, Putin said that he had informed Trump of Russia’s “readiness to supply oil and petroleum products to the US and global markets.” Putin did not offer any specifics, however, such as when a potential release would begin or how much fuel it would entail.

Since the start of the Iran war in February, the price of diesel fuel has soared almost 70%, and economists have warned that the price hikes will have wide-ranging inflationary effects on the global economy.
In recent weeks, sharp escalations in the Russia-Ukraine war have caused diesel to spike even further, and for multiple weeks the price of diesel set repeated all-time records.

title: Pope Leo to be hospitalized Tuesday for surgery to remove a lung nodule
summary: Pope Leo XIV will be admitted to a hospital Tuesday morning to undergo surgery to remove a lung nodule discovered during recent medical tests, the Vatican said Monday.
story: Pope Leo XIV will be admitted to a hospital Tuesday morning to undergo surgery to remove a lung nodule discovered during recent medical tests, the Vatican said Monday.
The timing of the procedure was confirmed after the 71-year-old American pontiff had a full day of meetings, audiences and appointments.
The Vatican press office also said no particular issue precipitated the tests, denying Italian media reports suggesting an inflammation had prompted the medical check-up.
